Agent Inbox is a helpdesk tool where support agents handle customer conversations across all channels (SMS, WhatsApp, email, chat). The API lets you extend it with custom data and integrations. ## Key capabilities - **Dynamic integration** — show customer info, orders, and profile data inside Agent Inbox - **Conversations retrieval** — access message history across channels - **Custom panels** — build custom UI panels visible to agents - **VoIP** — integrate voice calls into the agent workflow - **Channel API** — connect custom messaging channels - **Presence** — track agent availability in real-time - **CDP integration** — connect customer profiles to conversations ## Example: Retrieve conversations ```bash curl -X GET "https://api.cm.com/engagement/v1/conversations?status=open&limit=10" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" ``` ## Example: Dynamic integration panel Show custom customer data to your agents by providing a webhook URL. When an agent opens a conversation, Agent Inbox calls your endpoint to fetch relevant data: ```json { "webhook_url": "https://yourapi.com/agent-inbox/customer-panel", "display_name": "Order History" } ``` --- ## Campaigns & Email Marketing Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/campaigns.md Create, manage, and send marketing campaigns across SMS, email, and push channels. Track performance with detailed analytics. ## Key capabilities - **Campaign management** — create, update, send, pause, and resume campaigns - **Email campaigns** — templates, from addresses, mailing lists, and **webhooks** - **SMS campaigns** — bulk messaging with personalization - **Triggered drip campaigns** — automated campaign sequences based on events - **Senders** — manage sender identities - **Cost calculation** — estimate campaign costs before sending ## Example: Create a campaign ```bash curl -X POST https://api.cm.com/engagement/v1/campaigns \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "name": "Spring Sale 2026", "channel": "sms", "sender": "YourBrand", "message": "Spring sale! 20% off all items this weekend. Shop now: https://yourshop.com/sale", "audience_segment_id": "seg_active_customers" }' ``` ## Campaign lifecycle 1. **Draft** — configure message, audience, and schedule 2. **Scheduled** — campaign queued for delivery 3. **Sending** — messages being delivered 4. **Completed** — all messages sent 5. **Paused** — delivery temporarily halted (can be resumed) --- ## Customer Data Platform Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/cdp.md # Customer Data Platform (CDP) A **CDP** (Customer Data Platform) centralizes customer data from all touchpoints into a single profile. Use it to track interactions, build audience segments, and power personalized campaigns. ## Key capabilities - **Profiles** — create and manage customer profiles with custom attributes - **Events** — track customer interactions and behaviors - **Segmentation** — build audience segments based on profile data and events - **Email validation** — validate email addresses before adding to campaigns ## Example: Create a customer profile ```bash curl -X POST https://api.cm.com/engagement/v1/profiles \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "email": "jane@example.com", "first_name": "Jane", "last_name": "Doe", "phone": "+31612345678", "custom_attributes": { "plan": "premium", "signup_date": "2026-01-15" } }' ``` ## Example: Track an event ```bash curl -X POST https://api.cm.com/engagement/v1/events \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "profile_id": "prof_abc123", "event_type": "purchase", "properties": { "order_id": "ORD-5678", "amount": 49.99, "currency": "EUR" } }' ``` --- ## Chatbot & Routing Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/chatbot-routing.md Automate customer conversations with scripted chatbots and route messages intelligently between bots and live agents. ## How routing works The Conversational Router sits between your messaging channels and your response handlers (bots or agents). When a message arrives: 1. **Router evaluates rules** — checks channel, keywords, time of day, agent availability 2. **Routes to handler** — sends to the appropriate chatbot or live agent queue 3. **Handover when needed** — if the bot can't help, it escalates to a human agent ## Key capabilities - **Scripted chatbot** — build rule-based conversation flows - **Conversational Router** — route messages between channels, bots, and agents - **Live agent handover** — seamlessly escalate from bot to human agent - **Channel support** — works across all messaging channels ## Example: Configure a routing rule ```json { "rule": "after-hours", "condition": { "time": { "after": "18:00", "before": "09:00" } }, "action": { "route_to": "chatbot", "fallback": "voicemail" } } ``` ## Handover flow When a chatbot detects it can't resolve a customer's issue, it triggers a handover to a live agent in Agent Inbox. The agent sees the full conversation history so the customer doesn't have to repeat themselves. --- ## Customer Engagement Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement.md Everything you need to engage customers — from helpdesk integrations and marketing campaigns to customer data management and behavior tracking. ## [Webtracker](https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/webtracker) — website visitor tracking - [Chatbot & Routing](https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/chatbot-routing) — automated conversations --- ## AI Insights Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/adherence.md AI Insights shows you how many times agents used the AI suggestions they received during conversations. This is different from your quality score — it specifically tracks "Did the agent use the AI's suggested reply?" :::info This feature is only available if your account has it enabled. ::: ## How it works When agents are chatting with customers, the AI suggests helpful replies. AI Insights tracks: - How many suggestions the AI made - How many the agent actually used ## View AI Insights 1. Go to **AI Insights** in the left menu 2. You'll see a breakdown of how well agents used suggestions: - **Excellent** — agent used suggestions most of the time - **Good** — agent used suggestions regularly - **Fair** — agent used some suggestions - **Weak** — agent rarely used suggestions - **Poor** — agent didn't use suggestions \[AI Insights view] ## Check a specific conversation Click on a conversation to see: - How many suggestions were offered - How many were used - The actual suggestions and what the agent did \[AI Insights details] ## Filter results Filter by: - Date range - Channel (email, chat, phone, etc.) - Agent or team - Department This helps you find patterns — for example, "Chat agents use suggestions more than email agents" or "Tuesday conversations have lower usage" --- ## Assign scorecards Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/assignments.md Use different quality scorecards for different channels (email, chat, phone) or departments if they have different quality standards. ## Why do this? Different channels have different needs: - **Email support** — needs clarity and detailed answers - **Chat support** — needs speed and quick solutions - **Sales calls** — needs relationship building and product knowledge So you might use different scorecards for each. ## How it works 1. You pick which channels/departments get which scorecard 2. Conversations are automatically scored with the right scorecard 3. You see performance separately for each ## Set up assignments 1. Go to **Assignments** in the left menu 2. Choose **Channels** or **Departments** (two tabs) 3. Find the channel or department 4. Pick a scorecard from the dropdown 5. It saves automatically \[Assignments interface] \[Assigning a scorecard] ## Channel vs. Department - **Channels** — how customers reach you (email, chat, phone, etc.) - **Departments** — your internal teams (sales, support, billing, etc.) If you set up both: - Channel assignment wins (takes priority) - If no channel assignment, department assignment is used - If neither, the default scorecard is used ## Examples **By channel:** - Email → "Detailed Support" scorecard - Chat → "Quick Support" scorecard - Phone → "Personal Support" scorecard **By department:** - Sales team → "Relationship Building" scorecard - Support team → "Problem-solving" scorecard - Billing → "Accuracy & Compliance" scorecard ## Edit or remove Click the scorecard dropdown to: - Pick a different scorecard - Remove the assignment (leave blank) ## What you'll see After you set up assignments: - Each conversation is scored with the right scorecard - Dashboards show performance separately per channel - Reports break down results by scorecard used --- ## Define quality categories Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/categories.md Categories are the things you want to measure in conversations. For example: "Was the agent polite?" or "Did the agent solve the problem?" ## Examples of categories - **Politeness** — was the agent friendly and respectful? - **Problem-solving** — did the agent fix the customer's issue? - **Knowledge** — did the agent know the product/policy? - **Speed** — did the agent resolve it quickly? - **Clarity** — did the agent explain things clearly? You can create any categories that matter to your business. ## Create a category 1. Go to **Categories** in the left menu 2. Click **Create category** 3. Fill in: - **Name** — what you're measuring (e.g., "Politeness") - **Description** — explain what this means (optional) - **How to score it** — pick one: - **Yes/No** — agent either did it or didn't (e.g., "Did agent apologize?") - **Ratings** — pick a scale (e.g., 1-5 stars, with descriptions for each level) \[Categories list view] ## Example: Creating a Yes/No category **Name:** "Resolved the issue" **Description:** "Customer's problem was solved or next steps were clear" **How to score:** Yes / No --- ## Example: Creating a rated category **Name:** "Politeness" **Description:** "Agent was respectful and professional" **How to score:** Rating scale 1-5 - **1 (Poor):** Agent was rude or dismissive - **2 (Below Average):** Agent was neutral but slightly impatient - **3 (Good):** Agent was professional and friendly - **4 (Very Good):** Agent was warm and engaging - **5 (Excellent):** Agent went above and beyond to be helpful ## Edit or delete a category - **Edit** — Click the category to make changes. Changes apply everywhere you use it. - **Delete** — You can only delete categories you're not using. If you try to delete one that's in use, the system will tell you which scorecards use it. \[Edit category form] ## Tips - Keep category names simple and clear (one word is ideal) - Use Yes/No for things that either happened or didn't - Use ratings for things that can be "better" or "worse" - Create categories that matter to your customers and your business - You can reuse categories across different scorecards --- ## Review and score conversations Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/conversations-review.md Review individual conversations and score them based on your quality standards. You can agree with the automatic score or change it if you think something was scored wrong. ## 1. Open the conversations list Go to **Conversations** in the side navigation. Use the filter bar to narrow the list by period, channel, feedback, team, department (webstore), or a free-text search. Open a conversation Click a row, or use the row's actions menu → **Review**, to open the conversation. ## 3. Read the transcript and AI scores The review screen shows the full transcript next to the scoring panel. Each **focus area** groups the **categories** from the assigned scorecard; each category shows either: - a **Binary** rating (e.g. Yes/No, Satisfied/Unsatisfied), or - a **Numeric** rating (an ordered scale of levels) Scores the AI already produced show a blue **AI** tag. \[Conversation review with ratings] ## 4. Override a score or add feedback Click any category's rating to override the AI's score — the AI tag disappears once a human value is set. Feedback per profile is capped at 100 words. Save or approve - **Save** stores the review as a draft (`saved`). - **Approve** marks the review as final (`approved`). ## 6. Toggle **View Original** / **View Translated** in the feedback panel to switch back. --- ## Dashboard and analytics Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/dashboard.md Your dashboard shows how your team is doing — overall quality scores, which agents are top performers, and where to focus coaching. ## See your stats 1. Use this to: - Recognize top performers - Have them mentor lower-scoring agents - Understand what they're doing right ## Download or email a report - **Download PDF** — save the dashboard as a PDF to share or print - **Email report** — send to your manager or coaching team For automatic weekly or monthly reports sent to your inbox, see [Settings → Report scheduling](https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/settings/report-scheduling). --- ## Save great conversation examples Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/examples.md Save conversations that are scored perfectly (or poorly) to create a training library for your team. This shows agents what "good" looks like, and helps new team members learn your standards. ## Why save examples? - **Train new agents** — show them great conversations to emulate - **Share standards** — demonstrate what "excellent" really means - **Coaching reference** — point to real examples when coaching agents - **Improve scoring** — helps the system better understand your quality standards ## Save an example ### Option 1: Save from a conversation you already reviewed 1. Open any [conversation](https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/conversations-review) you've reviewed 2. Click the menu (three dots) in the header 3. Select **Save as example** 4. It saves with the score you gave it \[Save example from conversation] ### Option 2: Create a new example from scratch 1. Go to **Examples** in the left menu 2. Click **Create example** 3. Manually enter a conversation or paste it in 4. Score it just like you would a regular conversation 5. Save it \[Create example from scratch] ## View your examples Go to **Examples** to see all the conversations you've saved as references. Click one to see how it was scored and what feedback was given. \[Your saved examples] ## Update examples Keep your examples current: - If you change your scorecard, review your old examples - Delete examples that no longer match your standards - Add new examples as your team improves ## Share examples with your team Your team can view examples to understand: - What excellent looks like - What poor looks like - Real conversations, not just theory --- ## Onboarding Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/onboarding.md Place order in CM Orders. --- ## Build your scorecard Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/scorecards.md A scorecard is your quality checklist. It lists all the things you want to measure in a conversation and how important each one is. Think of it like a grading rubric for conversations. ## What goes in a scorecard A scorecard contains: - **Quality areas** — groups of related things to measure (e.g., "Customer Service", "Product Knowledge") - **Categories** — the individual things you measure (e.g., "Was the agent polite?") - **Importance** — how much each category matters in your overall score (e.g., is politeness worth 10% or 20%?) ## Example scorecard **Name:** Support Team Quality **Quality Areas:** 1. **Customer Service** (40% of total score) - Politeness (10%) - Response time (15%) - Empathy (15%) 2. **Problem-solving** (60% of total score) - Issue resolved (35%) - Follow-up provided (15%) - Knowledge demonstrated (10%) ## Create a scorecard 1. Go to **Scorecards** in the left menu 2. Click **Create scorecard** 3. Give it a name (e.g., "Support Team Quality") 4. (Optional) Add a description \[Scorecard list view] ## Add quality areas and categories 1. In the scorecard builder, click **Add quality area** 2. Give it a name (e.g., "Customer Service") 3. Click **Add category** to add items to measure 4. Pick from your existing [categories](https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/categories) 5. Set how important this category is (the system auto-calculates total importance) \[Edit scorecard interface] \[Creating quality area in scorecard] ## Set passing score (optional) Set what score counts as "passing" — for example, 70% or higher is good, below 70% needs coaching. ## Make it your default Check **Use as default scorecard** if this is the quality standard for your whole team. This scorecard will be used for any channel or department that doesn't have its own scorecard. ## Save your scorecard Click **Save**. Your scorecard is now ready to use for scoring conversations. ## Edit your scorecard You can change your scorecard anytime — add new categories, adjust importance levels, etc. Old conversations keep their original scores. Only new conversations will use the updated scorecard. ## Tips - Start simple with 5-7 categories (you can add more later) - Make sure your importance levels add up to 100% - Use the same categories across different scorecards when possible (makes comparison easier) - Have different scorecards for different channels if they have different standards (e.g., email vs. chat) --- ## Set up automatic reports Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/settings/report-scheduling.md Get your quality dashboard sent to your email automatically — weekly, twice a month, or monthly. ## How to create a scheduled report 1. Go to **Settings → Reports** tab 2. Choose a cadence: - **Weekly** — pick a day of the week - **Fortnightly** — 1st and 15th of each month - **Monthly** — 1st of each month 3. Click **Save schedule** The first report runs at the configured time, then repeats on the interval. ## What's included in each report Every scheduled report contains: - **Dashboard summary widgets** - Total conversations scored in the period - Average score with trend indicator - Score trends over time (line chart) - **Coaching heatmap** - Average score per agent × category - Identifies low-scoring combinations at a glance - **Agent leaderboard** - Top 5 agents by average score - Medal badges for 1st–3rd place All metrics reflect current account data (not a snapshot). Filters applied to report settings carry through to each delivery. ## Scheduling options ### Weekly - Runs every selected day at 00:00 UTC - Example: "Every Monday at 00:00 UTC" ### Fortnightly - Runs on the 1st and 15th of each month at 00:00 UTC - Example: "1st and 15th at 00:00 UTC" ### Monthly - Runs on the 1st of each month at 00:00 UTC - Example: "1st of each month at 00:00 UTC" \[Scheduled reports configuration] ## Managing your schedule **View next delivery:** Look for "Next delivery" date displayed after saving — confirms the schedule is active. **Change cadence:** Select a new cadence and click Save. The new schedule takes effect immediately. **Stop reports:** Clear the cadence selection and save. No further reports will be sent. ## Filters & recipients - Report metrics reflect the account's current data (not filtered by channel/team unless applied in Settings) - Recipients are configured separately in the Reports tab - Recipients receive the PDF report via email at the scheduled time ## Tips - Test with weekly cadence first to review report format - Adjust cadence to match your coaching cycle (weekly for active coaching, monthly for summary reviews) - Share reports with team leads for channel/department-level coaching --- ## Sync limiter Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/settings/sync-limiter.md Sync limiter lets you try out Quality Assurance with controlled conversation volumes. Test the platform without syncing your entire conversation history — sync a subset to learn the platform, build scorecards, and evaluate features. :::info **Trial/test accounts only.** Use sync limiter to evaluate QA with controlled data volumes. ::: ## Why sync limiter matters When trying out QA: - **Don't want 10k conversations on day 1** — start small, learn the platform - **Want to test specific channels** — sync only support team conversations first - **Need to control costs** — limit volume to your evaluation budget - **Want quality over quantity** — focus on understanding the tool Sync limiter lets you do all this. ## Sync modes Choose one mode that fits your evaluation: ### Conversation count mode Cap total conversations synced per day (1–100), newest first. **Good for:** Testing with a fixed daily volume. **How it works:** - Set daily limit (e.g., "50 conversations per day") - System syncs the newest conversations first - Limit applies to all agents in account - Counter resets every 24 hours (UTC) - Once limit is reached, older conversations are not synced **Example:** Set limit to 30/day, evaluate a small set each morning, build rubrics gradually. ### Agent sync mode Manually select which agents' conversations to sync. All conversations from selected agents are synced; others skipped. **Good for:** Testing with specific teams or departments. **How it works:** - Click agents to include or exclude from sync - Sync is unlimited per selected agent - Useful for department-focused trials (e.g., "just the support team") - Add/remove agents anytime to shift focus **Example:** Enable only 3 support agents, evaluate their conversations in detail, then add more agents later. ## Switching modes 1. Go to **Settings → Sync Limiter** tab 2. Choose a mode: - **Conversation count** — set daily limit (1–100) - **Agent sync** — select agents from list 3. Save Changes take effect immediately for new conversations. \[Sync limiter configuration] ## How it works ### Daily reset (conversation count mode) The 24-hour sync window resets at midnight UTC. If your limit is 50/day: - **Day 1:** 50 newest conversations sync by 23:59 UTC - **Day 2 (00:00 UTC):** counter resets, next 50 sync - **Older conversations:** never synced if Day 1 limit was reached ### Agent selection (agent sync mode) - **Selected agents:** all conversations synced, unlimited volume - **Unselected agents:** no conversations synced - **Switching agents:** takes effect for new conversations only ## Monitoring what synced - Go to **Settings → Details** to check sync status and connection health - Open **Conversations** tab to see what was synced (filter by date to see recent sync) - Check **Dashboard** to count synced conversations in your evaluation period ## Tips for trial evaluation **Week 1:** Use conversation count mode, set to 20/day. Learn the UI, build first categories & scorecard. **Week 2:** Increase to 40/day. Start reviewing & scoring. Calibrate with examples. **Week 3:** Switch to agent sync mode. Enable 2-3 more agents. Run coaching workflows. **Week 4:** Test scheduled reports, dashboards, team uploads. Ready to decide on production tier. --- ## Upload your team Source: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/quality-assurance-msc/settings/teams.md Upload your team/agent list from an Excel file so your dashboards can filter by team and agent. ## Get started 1. Go to **Settings → Teams** tab 2. Click **Download template** to get the Excel file 3. Fill it in with your team info 4. Download the template again 2. Update it with new info 3. Re-upload Existing conversations keep their team/agent association. --- ## Customer Engagement API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/customer-engagement/v1/api-reference Base URL: `https://api.cm.com` ### GET /engagement/v1/health Health check Verify that the Customer Engagement API is reachable and your credentials are valid. --- # Email Gateway API > Send transactional and marketing emails with delivery tracking, scheduling, and webhook support. --- ## Receive Emails Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails.md Receive email sent to addresses on your own domain. Every message is accepted, stored, and pushed to your application as a signed JSON `POST`. The webhook carries the full message (bodies and attachments), so you do not need a follow-up call to read it. Stored messages can also be browsed in the Email App (see [Dashboard](#dashboard)). ## Quickstart 1. **Enable receiving on a domain.** Add the receiving MX record, switch on the `receiving` capability and verify it. See [Receive Email on a Domain](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/email-domains#receive-email-on-a-domain). 2. **Send a test message** to any address at the domain, for example `support@your-domain.com`. 3. **Handle the request.** Verify the signature, process the JSON, and answer with a `2xx` within 10 seconds. See [Verify and delivery](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/verify-and-delivery). ## In this section | Page | What it covers | | - | - | | [Webhook payload](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/webhook-payload) | JSON body, attachments (inline or download links), size limits, HTML sanitisation. | | [Verify and delivery](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/verify-and-delivery) | Request headers, signature verification, idempotency, failures and replay. | ## Dashboard The Email App lists received emails with sender, recipient, subject and timestamp, and supports search plus timezone and time-range filters. A **Receiving Address** option in the page menu shows the addresses you can receive on. Open a message to see its details and these tabs: | Tab | Shown | Content | | - | - | - | | Preview | Always | Rendered message, with inline `cid:` images resolved. | | Text | When the message has a plain-text body | The text body. | | HTML | When the message has an HTML body | The sanitised HTML source. | | Raw | Always | The stored record as JSON. | Attachments are listed on the message and download on click. Domain capability toggles and the MX conflict warning are on the domain detail page. --- ## Send Marketing Email Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/send-marketing-index.md The Marketing Email API is designed for sending high-volume email campaigns to your subscribers. It allows you to send promotional emails, newsletters, and other marketing content to engage your audience effectively. For one-to-one, event- of system driven emails like purchase confirmations or password recovery requests, please refer to our [Transactional Email API documentation](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/send-transactional-index/). ## Authentication To interact with the Marketing Email API, you need a secret key called the Product Token. Once you have access to the Email App, you can retrieve the Product Token by navigating to the Settings page within the app and copying the token. When making a request to the Marketing Email API, include the Product Token in the request headers. Specifically, add it as a header with the key name `X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN` in your POST request. ## Request Headers ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/marketing Content-Type: application/json X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: {your-product-token} ``` | Header Name | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN | string | Yes | Valid product token GUID | | Content-Type | string | Yes | Must be "application/json" | ## Request Example The example provided below demonstrates the most basic structure of an Email message request. ```json { "from": { "email": "sender@example.com", "name": "Sender Name" }, "replyTo": { "email": "reply@example.com", "name": "Reply Name" }, "to": [ { "email": "recipient@example.com", "name": "Recipient Name" } ], "cc": [ { "email": "cc@example.com", "name": "CC Name" } ], "bcc": [ { "email": "bcc@example.com", "name": "BCC Name" } ], "subject": "Email Subject", "html": "

HTML content (optional)

", "text": "Plain text content (optional)", "attachments": [ { "fileName": "document.pdf", "content": "base64-encoded-content", "contentType": "application/pdf", "contentId": "attachment-id" } ], "customerReference": "your-reference" } ``` ## Successful Response ```json { "status": 202, "message": "Accepted", "success": true, "messageId": "5dcdf71f-96d6-4763-8d70-ef17d8aa6dbc" } ``` For all response codes see the [response codes](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/response-codes) page. ## Custom Unsubscribe Link The Email Gateway automatically includes a standard unsubscribe link at the end of all marketing emails. However, you can customize the placement using the `{{{unsubscribe_link}}}` placeholder: ```html

If you no longer wish to receive these emails, click here to unsubscribe.

``` When the email is sent, the system will replace the placeholder with the recipient's unique unsubscribe link. If the placeholder is not included, the system will append the default unsubscribe link to the end of your email content to ensure compliance with email marketing regulations. By using the `{{{unsubscribe_link}}}` placeholder, you can control exactly where the unsubscribe link appears in your email, giving you more flexibility in designing your email content. ## Test Your Integration If you want to test your integration or see how quickly you can send multiple messages through the Email Gateway without affecting your reputation, you can use the Email Gateway' Sandbox or Integration mode. - [Sandbox Mode:](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/test-your-integration#sandbox-mode) Verify and validate your integration and requests without sending messages. - [Integration Mode](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/test-your-integration#integration-mode): Tests the complete workflow and speed without sending messages. --- ## Best Practices 1. **Clear Subject Lines**: Make subjects descriptive and actionable 2. **Customer References**: Use meaningful reference IDs for tracking and debugging 3. **Content Size**: Keep total email size under 25MB including all attachments 4. **Recipient Validation**: Ensure all email addresses are properly formatted --- ## Send Transactional Email Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/send-transactional-index.md The Transactional Email API is designed for sending event-driven emails that require immediate delivery. These emails are typically triggered by user actions or system events, such as sign-ups, purchase confirmations, or password recovery requests. If you're looking to send bulk promotional emails or newsletters, please use the [Marketing Email API documentation](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/send-marketing-index/). ## Authentication To interact with the Transactional Email API, you need a secret key called the Product Token. Once you have access to the Email App, you can retrieve the Product Token by navigating to the Settings page within the app and copying the token. When making a request to the Transactional Email API, include the Product Token in the request headers. Specifically, add it as a header with the key name `X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN` in your POST request. ## Request Headers ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/transactional?priority={priority} Content-Type: application/json X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: {your-product-token} ``` | Header Name | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN | string | Yes | Valid product token GUID | | Content-Type | string | Yes | Must be "application/json" | The Transactional Email API also expects a priority value in the query parameter which can either be Low or High. | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | priority | string | Yes | "low" or "high" | ## Request Example The example provided below demonstrates the most basic structure of an Email message request. ```json { "from": { "email": "sender@example.com", "name": "Sender Name" }, "replyTo": { "email": "reply@example.com", "name": "Reply Name" }, "to": [ { "email": "recipient@example.com", "name": "Recipient Name" } ], "cc": [ { "email": "cc@example.com", "name": "CC Name" } ], "bcc": [ { "email": "bcc@example.com", "name": "BCC Name" } ], "subject": "Email Subject", "html": "

HTML content (optional)

", "text": "Plain text content (optional)", "attachments": [ { "fileName": "document.pdf", "content": "base64-encoded-content", "contentType": "application/pdf", "contentId": "attachment-id" } ], "customerReference": "your-reference" } ``` ## Successful Response ```json { "status": 202, "message": "Accepted", "success": true, "messageId": "5dcdf71f-96d6-4763-8d70-ef17d8aa6dbc" } ``` For all response codes see the [response codes](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/response-codes) page. ## Test Your Integration If you want to test your integration or see how quickly you can send multiple messages through the Email Gateway without affecting your reputation, you can use the Email Gateway' Sandbox or Integration mode. - [Sandbox Mode:](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/test-your-integration#sandbox-mode) Verify and validate your integration and requests without sending messages. - [Integration Mode](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/test-your-integration#integration-mode): Tests the complete workflow and speed without sending messages. ## Best Practices 1. **Priority Usage**: Use "high" priority only for truly time-sensitive emails 2. **Clear Subject Lines**: Make subjects descriptive and actionable 3. **Customer References**: Use meaningful reference IDs for tracking and debugging 4. **Content Size**: Keep total email size under 25MB including all attachments 5. **Recipient Validation**: Ensure all email addresses are properly formatted --- ## Webhooks Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/webhooks.md Use webhooks to push real-time email notifications to your application. All webhooks use HTTPS and deliver a JSON payload that can be used by your application. ## Add/Update Webhook Register new or update existing webhooks to receive email event notifications. ### Request Header ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/webhook/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/create Content-Type: application/json ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | Header Name | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | Content-Type | string | Yes | Must be "application/json" | | Authorization | string | Yes | Valid authorization token | ### Request Body ```json { "webhookType": "delivered", "webhookUrl": "https://your-domain.com/webhook/email-events" } ``` Use one of the following supported webhook types: | Webhook Type | Enum Value | Description | Events Included | | - | - | - | - | | global | 0 | All email events | All email events in single webhook | | delivered | 1 | Successful email deliveries | Email delivered to recipient's inbox | | opened | 2 | Email opens | Recipient opened the email | | clicked | 3 | Email link clicks | Recipient clicked on email links | | bounced | 4 | Email bounces (hard and soft) | Failed delivery attempts | | unsubscribed | 5 | Unsubscribe events | Recipient unsubscribed | | complained | 6 | Spam complaints | Email marked as spam | | failed | 7 | Email send failures | Email failed to send | | sent | 8 | Email sent successfully | Email accepted and sent from server | | suppressed | 9 | Suppressed emails | Email suppressed from sending | ### Response Body ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Successfully created/updated webhook with id 148", "data": 148 } ``` ### Errors Responses **Invalid Request Body (400)** ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Provide a valid url for webhook.", "data": 0 } ``` **Invalid Account ID (400)** ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Logical account id is not valid.", "data": 0 } ``` **Invalid Webhook Type (400)** ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Invalid webhook type: opened1", "data": 0 } ``` **Invalid Webhook URL (400)** ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Provide a valid url for webhook.", "data": 0 } ``` ## Get Webhook Retrieve webhook configuration for a specific account and webhook type. ### Request Header ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/webhook/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/list?webhookType={webhookType} ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | webhookType | string | No | Specific webhook type to retrieve (e.g., "delivered", "bounced") | ### Response Body **Successful Response - Specific Webhook (200)** ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Successfully retrieved webhook for account 50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b and type 1", "data": { "webhookType": 1, "url": "https://webhook.site/547a4f29-49a2-4d06-98db-2a721b563f01" } } ``` **Successful Response - No Webhook Found (200)** ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Webhook type not found.", "data": null } ``` **Successful Response - Webhook Types (200)** When `webhookType` is empty or "-1", returns available webhook types: ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Successfully retrieved webhook type for account 50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "data": "global" } ``` ### Error Responses #### Invalid Account ID (400) ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Invalid account ID provided", "data": null } ``` #### Webhook Not Found (404) ```json { "success": false, "status": 404, "message": "Webhook type not found", "data": null } ``` ## Delete Webhook Remove a webhook configuration for a specific account and webhook type. ### Request Header ```http DELETE https://api.cm.com/email/webhook/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/delete?webhookType={webhookType} ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | webhookType | string | Yes | Webhook type to delete (e.g., "delivered", "bounced", "clicked") | ### Response Body Successful Response (200)\*\* ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Successfully deleted 1 webhook(s)", "success": true } ``` **Successful Response - No Webhook Found (200)** ```json { "status": 200, "message": "No webhook found to delete", "success": true } ``` ### Error Responses **Invalid Account ID (400)** ```json { "status": 400, "message": "Invalid account Id provided", "success": false } ``` **Invalid Webhook Type (400)** ```json { "status": 400, "message": "Invalid webhook type: bounced1", "success": false } ``` ## Request Parameters ### Request Body Fields | Field | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | webhookType | string | Yes | Type of webhook: "global", "delivered", "opened", "clicked", "bounced", "unsubscribed", "complained", "failed", "sent", "suspended" | | webhookUrl | string | Yes | HTTPS URL endpoint to receive webhook notifications | ### Response Object | Field | Type | Description | | - | - | - | | webhookType | string | Type of webhook events | | url | string | Configured webhook endpoint URL | ### Webhook URL Requirements | Requirement | Description | | - | - | | Protocol | Must use HTTPS for security | | Accessibility | Must be publicly accessible from CM servers | | Response | Should respond with 200 status for successful receipt | ### Status Codes | Status Code | Description | | - | - | | 200 | OK: Request processed successfully | | 400 | Bad Request: Invalid request data or parameters | | 404 | Not Found: Requested webhook not found | | 500 | Internal Server Error: Server-side error | ## Event Payload Structure **When events occur, webhooks will receive POST requests with payloads like:** ```json { "type": "string", "createdAt": "string", "messageId": "GUID string", "data": { "to": "string", "from": "string", "id": "GUID string", "customerReference": "string", "unsubscribe": { "type": "string", "message": "string" }, "bounce": { "type": "string", "subType": "string", "message": "string" }, "failed": { "messages": [ "string 1", "string 2" ] } } } ``` For all webhook events, see our [Event Types page](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/webhooks/event-types). To confirm a request came from CM.com, see [Webhook Verification](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/webhooks/webhook-verification). ## Multi-Webhook Setup Example Configure different webhooks for different event types: ```bash # Delivery tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "delivered", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/delivered" } # Sent tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "sent", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/sent" } # Bounce management POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "bounced", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/bounces" } # Open tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "opened", "webhookUrl": "https://analytics.your-app.com/email-opens" } # Click tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "clicked", "webhookUrl": "https://analytics.your-app.com/email-clicks" } # Unsubscribe handling POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "unsubscribed", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/unsubscribes" } # Spam report monitoring POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "complained", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/spam-reports" } # Failed email tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "failed", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/failed" } # Suppressed email tracking POST /v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/create { "webhookType": "suppressed", "webhookUrl": "https://your-app.com/webhooks/suppressed" } ``` --- ## Email Gateway API Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api.md Send transactional and marketing emails, manage domains, configure webhooks, and monitor usage — all through a single REST API. ## Base URL The Email Gateway API is built on REST principles. To prioritize security, **HTTPS is mandatory** for all requests, and **HTTP is not supported**. All requests contain the following base URL: `https://api.cm.com/email/` ## Authentication To authenticate you will need a secure credential called the **Product Token**. This token acts as your unique key to authenticate requests. How to Obtain the Product Token: - Log in to the Email Gateway App. - Navigate to the **Settings** page within the app. - Locate and copy your Product Token in the **Integration** section. When making a request to the API, include the Product Token in the request headers. Use the header name `X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN` and pass the token as its value. For example, in a POST request, your header should look like this: ```curl curl -X POST "https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/transactional?priority={priority}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: {your-product-token}" \ -d '{your-json-payload}' ``` ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/transactional?priority={priority} Content-Type: application/json X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: {your-product-token} ``` ## Response Codes The API follows standard HTTP status codes to communicate the outcome of your requests. Here's a breakdown of how these codes are used: - `2xx`: Indicates a successful request. - `4xx`: Represents client-side errors, such as invalid input or authentication issues. - `5xx`: Signals server-side errors or infrastructure problems. | Status | Meaning | | :- | :- | | `200` | Request was successful. | | `400` | Invalid parameters; check your input. | | `401` | Missing Product Token. | | `403` | Invalid Product Token. | | `404` | Resource not found. | | `429` | Rate limit exceeded. | | `5xx` | Server error on CM.com's side. | These codes help you quickly identify and troubleshoot issues with your API requests. ## API Reference Explore detailed endpoint documentation in the **API Reference** section, organized by feature: - **Send Email** — POST transactional and marketing messages - **Email Configuration** — Manage domains and DNS settings - **Webhooks** — Configure event notifications - **Usage Alerts** — Monitor email consumption - **Suppressions** — Manage bounces and unsubscribes --- ## Changelog Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/changelog.md ## Breaking Change: Received Email Attachment IDs Are UUIDs **Date:** 2026-11-04 - The `id` of an attachment returned by the received-email endpoints (attachment list, email details and email list) is now a UUID string. - Update any code that stores or parses this `id` as an integer. ## Breaking Change: Domain and Receiving Webhook API Updates **Date:** 2026-10-03 - List domains moved to `GET /configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains`. Each added domain includes automatically generated DNS records for proper email delivery. ## Add Domain Register a domain. CM.com generates its DNS records: three CNAME records for sending and one MX record for receiving. Sending is enabled and receiving is disabled for a new domain, so add the MX record to your DNS if you want to [receive email on this domain](#receive-email-on-a-domain). ### Request ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/add-domain Content-Type: application/json ``` | **Header Name** | **Type** | **Required** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | Content-Type | string | Yes | Must be "application/json" | ```json { "accountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "domain": "example.com", "clickTracking": false, "openTracking": false } ``` ### Response Body #### Successful Response (200) ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Success", "success": true, "domainConfig": { "id": "9f0b5c3e-6a1d-4c8e-b7a2-3d5e1f4a8c90", "accountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "domain": "example.com", "createdOn": null, "modifiedOn": null, "deletedOn": null, "dnsRecords": [], "isValid": false, "clickTracking": false, "openTracking": false, "sendingEnabled": false, "receivingEnabled": false, "status": "NotStarted" } } ``` The create response does not populate the timestamps, `sendingEnabled`, `receivingEnabled`, `status` or the per-record `dnsStatus`. Read the stored state with [Get Domains](#get-domains). The record values above are illustrative. The value suffix depends on the environment, so always copy the records from the response. ### Error Responses | Status | Message | Cause | | - | - | - | | 400 | `Domain cannot be empty` | `domain` is blank. | | 400 | `Domain exceeds maximum length of 253 characters` | `domain` is too long. | | 400 | `Invalid domain format` | `domain` is not a valid host name. | | 400 | `Domain '{domain}' already exists for this account` | The account already has this domain. | | 400 | `Invalid request. Please check your input.` | `accountId` is not a valid account token. | | 403 | `Trial accounts are limited to a single domain` | A trial account already has a domain. | | 409 | `Domain '{domain}' conflicts with a domain already in use by another account` | Trial accounts only: another account already registered this domain. | | 500 | `Unable to create Domain` | The domain could not be stored. | Every error uses the same envelope with `success: false`: ```json { "status": 403, "message": "Trial accounts are limited to a single domain", "success": false, "domainConfig": null } ``` ## Get Domains Retrieve all domain configurations for a specific logical account. ### Request Header ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains ``` | **Parameter** | **Type** | **Required** | **Description** | | - Please check your input.` | `logicalAccountId` is empty. | | 400 | `Unable to get the domain config` | The domains could not be read. | | 500 | `Unable to get the domain config` | Unexpected failure while reading. | ```json { "status": 500, "message": "Unable to get the domain config", "domains": [], "success": false } ``` ## Get DNS Records Retrieve DNS records for a specific domain within an account. ### Request Header ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domainId} ``` | **Parameter** | **Type** | **Required** | **Description** | | - | - | - | | 400 | `Unable to fetch DNS records` | The records could not be read. | | 500 | `Unable to fetch DNS records` | Unexpected failure while reading. | ## Delete Domain Remove a domain configuration and all associated DNS records. ### Request Header ```http DELETE https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domainId} ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | domainId | UUID | Yes | The domain identifier to delete | ### Response Body #### Successful Response (200) ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Success", "success": true } ``` ### Error Responses | Status | Message | Cause | | - | - | - | | 400 | `Invalid request. Please check your input.` | `logicalAccountId` is empty. | | 400 | `Unable to delete the domain` | No domain with this `domainId` exists on the account, or the delete failed. | | 404 | `The requested resource was not found.` | `domainId` is an empty UUID (all zeros). | ## Verify Domain Configuration Check the DNS records of every capability that is enabled on the domain. Sending is checked through its CNAME records, receiving through its MX record. To check one capability only, see [Verify a capability](#verify-a-capability). ### Request ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/dns/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/verify?domain={domain} Content-Type: application/json ``` | Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | path | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | domain | query | string | Yes | Domain name to verify (e.g., "example.com") | | Header Name | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | Authorization | string | Yes | Valid authorization token | ### Response Body #### Successful Response (200) `dnsEntries` lists every record on the domain: the three sending CNAMEs and the receiving MX. Each entry has `isValid` and a `status` (`1` not verified yet, `2` verified, `3` verification ran and failed). ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Success", "success": true, "dnsEntries": [ { "host": "cm50025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2b.example.com", "value": "50025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2b.email.cm.com.", "isValid": true, "type": "CNAME", "purpose": "sending", "priority": null, "status": 2 }, { "host": "cm150025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2b._domainkey.example.com", "value": "50025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2bcm1._domainkey.email.cm.com.", "isValid": true, "type": "CNAME", "purpose": "sending", "priority": null, "status": 2 }, { "host": "cm250025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2b._domainkey.example.com", "value": "50025f6ad4fd4a239e2ebbee1cf67d2bcm2._domainkey.email.cm.com.", "isValid": false, "type": "CNAME", "purpose": "sending", "priority": null, "status": 3 }, { "host": "example.com", "value": "mx.email.cm.com.", "isValid": false, "type": "MX", "purpose": "receiving", "priority": 10, "status": 3 } ] } ``` A `200` means the check ran, not that the domain is valid. Read `isValid` on each entry. Re-run the call after DNS has propagated. ### Error Responses Failures return `dnsEntries: []` and the message `unable to verify domain`. The `status` and HTTP code identify the cause. | Status | Cause | | - | - | | 400 | Domain is blank or the request is invalid. | | 401 | Missing or invalid credentials or permission. | | 404 | The domain is not registered on this account. | | 409 | Receiving is already enabled and verified for this domain under another account. See [One owner per domain](#one-owner-per-domain). | | 500 | The verification result could not be stored. | ## Receive Email on a Domain Receiving adds one **MX record** that routes mail for any address at the domain to CM.com. The endpoints in this section enable or disable each capability and verify it. They use the same base URL and authentication as the rest of this page. For what happens to a message once it arrives, see [Receive Emails](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails). The two capabilities are independent. Enabling receiving does not require you to re-verify sending, and only the MX record is checked for receiving. > **Use a dedicated subdomain if the domain already receives mail.** CM.com must be the most preferred MX for the domain, so adding it to a domain that hosts your regular mailboxes would redirect that mail. Register a subdomain such as `inbound.example.com` for inbound mail instead. ### Enable or disable a capability #### Enable or disable receiving ```http PUT https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domain}/receiving?enabled=true ``` #### Enable or disable sending ```http PUT https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domain}/sending?enabled=true ``` #### Parameters Both calls take the same parameters. | Parameter | In | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | - | | `logicalAccountId` | path | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier. | | `domain` | path | string | Yes | Domain name, max 253 characters. Matched exactly (case-sensitive) against the stored domain, which is lowercase. | | `enabled` | query | boolean | Yes | `true` to enable, `false` to disable. Always send it explicitly. | Sending is enabled by default for new domains; receiving is disabled. Toggling one capability leaves the other untouched. Enabling a capability triggers a best-effort DNS verification straight away, so the returned records may already be valid. A failure of that check does not fail the request. Disabling a capability stops its DNS records counting as valid. Disabling receiving therefore invalidates the MX record. #### Successful response (200) `data` holds the updated domain (single element). `status` is `NotStarted`, `Verified` or `Failed`. ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Success", "data": [ { "id": "9f0b5c3e-6a1d-4c8e-b7a2-3d5e1f4a8c90", "accountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "domain": "example.com", "isValid": false, "status": "NotStarted", "sendingEnabled": true, "receivingEnabled": true, "dnsRecords": [ { "host": "example.com", "type": "MX", "value": "mx.email.cm.com.", "purpose": "receiving", "priority": 10, "dnsStatus": "NotStarted" } ] } ] } ``` #### Error responses | Status | Message | Cause | | - | - | - | | 400 | `Domain length exceeded the max limit` | `domain` blank or longer than 253 characters. | | 401 | `Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid credentials / permission. | | 404 | `Domain not found` | Domain is not registered on this account. | | 409 | `Receiving is already enabled and verified for this domain under another account. Disable it there before enabling it here.` | Ownership rule, see [One owner per domain](#one-owner-per-domain). `receiving` with `enabled=true` only. | | 500 | `Something went wrong while toggling domain capabilities` | Write failed. | ### Verify a capability The [Verify Domain Configuration](#verify-domain-configuration) call checks every capability enabled on the domain. To check one capability, add it to the path: ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/configuration/v1/dns/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/verify/{capability}?domain={domain} ``` | Parameter | In | Description | | - | - | - | | `logicalAccountId` | path | The logical account identifier (UUID). | | `capability` | path | `sending`, `receiving` or `all` (case-insensitive). Anything else returns 400 `Invalid capability value`. | | `domain` | query | Domain name. Query parameter only, max 253 characters. | #### Successful response (200) Same `dnsEntries` shape as the plain verify call, with `purpose`, `priority` and `status` added to each entry: ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Success", "success": true, "dnsEntries": [ { "host": "example.com", "value": "mx.email.cm.com.", "isValid": true, "type": "MX", "purpose": "receiving", "priority": 10, "status": 2 } ] } ``` #### Error responses Same statuses as the errors under [Verify Domain Configuration](#verify-domain-configuration), with these messages: 400 `Domain name is invalid or exceeds the max limit. unable to verify domain`, 404 `No DNS records found for the specified domain`, 500 `Invalid domain host validity.`. The 409 is the [one-owner rule](#one-owner-per-domain). A change in the domain's overall verified state also sends a _Domain status change_ notification email to the account. ### One owner per domain Inbound routing is keyed on the domain's MX, so a delivered message must belong to exactly one account. At most **one** account can hold _enabled and verified_ receiving for a given domain (compared case-insensitively). - Enabling receiving (`PUT …/receiving?enabled=true`) returns **409 Conflict** straight away if another account already holds enabled and verified receiving for the domain. - Verifying receiving (`POST …/verify/receiving`) returns the same 409 if another account became the owner in the meantime. Only one account can ever be verified. - To move a domain, disable receiving on the current owner first, then enable and verify it on the new account. ### Automatic re-verification All domains are re-checked weekly, only for their enabled capabilities. A change in a domain's overall verified state emails the account. A check that cannot complete is skipped and leaves the stored state unchanged. ### In the Email App The domain detail page has a **Sending Enabled** and a **Receiving Enabled** toggle. The MX record appears in the receiving table with its priority. If the app detects a conflicting MX record it shows a warning, and a `409` from the ownership rule is reported as _"Another account has already enabled and verified receiving for this domain"_. The **Verify Domain** button checks every enabled capability. Verifying one capability on its own is available through the API only. ### Receiving setup checklist 1. [Add the domain](#add-domain). 2. Add the MX record returned in the API response to your domain's DNS. 3. Wait for DNS propagation, then call `POST …/verify/receiving?domain=…` until `isValid` is `true`. 4. Register an inbound webhook for the domain. 5. Send a test message to any address at the domain and check the **Receiving** page in the Email App. ## Domain Verification Process 1. **Add Domain**: Submit your account ID and the domain name 2. **DNS Records Generated**: System automatically creates three CNAME records for sending and one MX record for receiving. Add the MX record to your DNS if you want to [receive email on this domain](#receive-email-on-a-domain) 3. **Add DNS Records**: Add the generated CNAME records to your domain's DNS settings 4. **Wait for Propagation**: Allow time for DNS changes to propagate (5 minutes to 48 hours) 5. **Verify Domain**: Use the verification endpoint to check DNS record configuration 6. **Check Results**: Review verification response to see which records are valid 7. **Retry if Needed**: Re-run verification after additional propagation time if some records show as invalid 8. **Email Sending**: Domain is ready for email sending once all records show `"isValid": true` To receive inbound email on the domain, see [Receive Email on a Domain](#receive-email-on-a-domain) and [Receive Emails](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails). ## Common Issues and Solutions | Issue | Cause | Solution | | - | - | - | | All records show `isValid: false` | DNS records not yet added or propagated | Wait for DNS propagation (5 min - 48 hours) and retry | | Some records valid, others invalid | Partial DNS configuration or caching | Check DNS provider settings and wait for full propagation | | Verification endpoint returns 404 | Domain not found in account | Ensure domain was properly added to account first | | Verification endpoint returns 409 | Another account owns receiving for the domain | See [One owner per domain](#one-owner-per-domain) | ## Example Use Cases **Register Company Domain** Setting up a primary company domain for email sending: ```json { "accountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "domain": "company.com" } ``` **Add Subdomain for Marketing** Adding a subdomain specifically for marketing campaigns: ```json { "accountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "domain": "marketing.company.com" } ``` **Multi-Domain Setup** Managing multiple domains for different business units: 1. **Main Website**: `company.com` 2. **Support Portal**: `support.company.com` 3. **Marketing Campaigns**: `promo.company.com` 4. **Customer Portal**: `portal.company.com` Each domain receives the same three sending CNAME records (with domain-specific hostnames) plus one receiving MX record, all pointing to the same account-specific email infrastructure, ensuring consistent email delivery across all business units. --- ## Fact Sheet Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/fact-sheet.md ## Marketing Email | Feature | Support | Remark | | - Reserved system headers cannot be overridden. | --- ## Payment Options, Usage & Billing Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/payment-options-usage-billing.md This guide explains how billing works for the Email Gateway: the payment options available, what counts as a billable event, where to monitor your usage, and how invoicing works. ## Payment options There are four payment options. Which one applies to your account is set up during onboarding and shown in your account settings. | Plan | How it works | Billing model | Included volume | Overage | | - | - | - | - | - | | **Free account** | For testing and very low-volume sending | No cost | 1 domain, 100 emails/day | Sending is blocked once the daily limit is reached | | **Prepaid** | You top up a balance and send against it | Balance is deducted per accepted message | Determined by your balance, not a fixed volume | Sending stops when your balance runs out; top up to resume | | **Pay-as-you-go (PAYG)** | Postpaid: you send first, get billed after | Charged per bucket of 1,000 accepted messages | No fixed monthly volume | Not applicable: you're billed for actual usage each period | | **Bundles** | A fixed monthly fee for a set volume of emails | Fixed monthly fee, plus overage if you exceed the bundle | Fixed monthly allowance (set per contract) | Charged per bucket of 1,000 accepted messages sent over your monthly allowance | ### Free account - Hard-capped at **100 emails per day** and **1 sending domain**. - Intended for evaluation and low-volume use, not production traffic. - No invoicing: there's no cost associated with this plan. ### Prepaid - You add funds to a balance up front. - Each accepted message deducts from that balance in real time. - There's no fixed "monthly limit" in the same sense as Bundles. Your effective limit is however much balance you have available. - Once the balance is spent, sending is paused until you top up again. ### Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) - No prepayment or fixed allowance; you send, and usage is tallied. - Billed **per bucket of 1,000 accepted messages** sent in the billing period. - Because there's no fixed limit, there's no "overage" concept; all usage is simply billed. ### Bundles - You pay a fixed monthly fee for a set number of emails (your **monthly allowance**). - If you exceed your allowance in a given month, you're charged an **overage fee per bucket of 1,000 messages** sent above the limit. - Your remaining allowance and reset date are visible in the dashboard. See "Monitoring your usage" below. ## Billable events The billable event is the accepted message. A message only counts toward usage and billing once it has been accepted for delivery. - **Rejected messages are not charged.** If a message is rejected (for example, due to validation errors or a recipient on the suppression list), it does not count against your usage or your bill. - This applies consistently across all four payment options: Free, Prepaid, PAYG, and Bundles. ### Messages sent to `@sink.cm.com` If you send messages to an `@sink.cm.com` address while in **integration (test) mode**, be aware that: - These messages **do contribute to your monthly usage limit**, in the same way live traffic does. - If you're on a **pay-as-you-go plan**, these messages are counted as **billable usage**. You will be charged for them per the standard PAYG bucket pricing. In short: sending to `@sink.cm.com` is useful for validating your integration, but it is not "free" traffic from a usage or billing perspective. Plan your test volume accordingly, especially close to a billing period reset or a Bundle allowance limit. ## Monitoring your usage You can check your current usage at any time in the dashboard, at the bottom of the side navigation. This widget shows: - **Sender Score**: your current sending reputation score. - **Monthly Limit**: a progress bar showing messages sent vs. your monthly allowance (e.g. `128,722 / 500,000`). - **Reset In**: a countdown to when your usage resets, along with the reset date (e.g. `8 days (Oct 1, 2026)`). This is the fastest way to see how close you are to your monthly limit (Bundles) or how much usage has accrued so far in the current period (PAYG), without waiting for an invoice. ## Invoicing At the end of each billing period, CM.com generates an invoice based on your plan and actual usage in that period: - **Free accounts** are not invoiced; there is no associated cost. - **Prepaid accounts** are settled in real time as your balance is deducted, so there is no separate usage invoice. You'll instead see invoices for your balance top-ups. - **PAYG and Bundle accounts** receive an invoice reflecting the period's usage: for PAYG, total buckets of 1,000 accepted messages; for Bundles, the fixed monthly fee plus any overage buckets. --- ## Verify and Delivery Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/verify-and-delivery.md ## Request your endpoint receives ```http POST /inbound HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 svix-id: 9f2c…(64 hex chars) cm-message-id: abc123@mail.sender.example svix-timestamp: 1791452467123 svix-signature: Zm9vYmFy… ``` | Header | Description | | - | - | | `svix-id` | Lower-case hex SHA-256 identifying the message and recipient. **Not a UUID.** Stable across redeliveries, so use it as your idempotency key. | | `cm-message-id` | Canonicalised RFC Message-ID (no angle brackets). | | `svix-timestamp` | Unix time in **milliseconds** (Svix proper uses seconds). | | `svix-signature` | Base64 HMAC-SHA512, no `v1,` prefix. | ## Verify the signature ```text signature = base64( HMAC_SHA512( key = UTF8(secret), data = svix-id + "." + svix-timestamp + "." + rawBodyBytes ) ) ``` - The key is your **Webhook Secret** (Settings → Integration) used as raw UTF-8. Do not base64-decode it or strip a `whsec_` prefix. - Sign the **exact bytes** received. Do not parse and re-serialise. - This is the same scheme as outbound [event webhooks](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/webhooks), so one secret and one verifier cover both. A stock Svix library will reject it because of the millisecond timestamp. ```js const crypto = require('crypto'); function verify(secret, headers, rawBody /* Buffer */) { const mac = crypto.createHmac('sha512', secret) .update(`${headers['svix-id']}.${headers['svix-timestamp']}.`) .update(rawBody) .digest('base64'); const got = Buffer.from(headers['svix-signature'] || ''); const want = Buffer.from(mac); return got.length === want.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(got, want); } ``` Also reject stale `svix-timestamp` values (for example older than 5 minutes) to limit replay. **Unsigned deliveries.** If your account has no active webhook secret, requests are sent with only `svix-id` and `cm-message-id`. Create a secret to receive signed requests. If the secret cannot be read (transient error), the delivery is **not** made at all rather than sent unsigned. ## Respond Return any `2xx` status. CM.com waits up to 3 seconds to connect and 10 seconds in total. Respond quickly and process the message asynchronously. ## Failures and replay Delivery is **at-least-once**. Deduplicate on `svix-id`. - A timeout, connection error, `408`, `429` or `5xx` is a transient failure. Any other non-`2xx` (including a `3xx`) and a rejected URL is a permanent failure. - There is **no automatic retry**. Both kinds of failure hold the message for replay by CM.com. The message stays stored and visible in the Email App. - A replay only re-sends to the webhooks that did not succeed. A webhook that already returned `2xx` for the message is skipped for 24 hours, so replays do not normally duplicate deliveries to it. --- ## Webhook Payload Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/webhook-payload.md Each inbound email is sent as compact JSON. String fields that are empty are **omitted**; arrays are always present. ```json { "type": "Inbound", "logicalAccount": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "from": "jane@sender.example", "fromName": "Jane Doe", "to": "support@example.com", "originalRecipient": "support@example.com", "cc": [], "bcc": [], "subject": "Order #1234", "date": "Thu, 08 Oct 2026 11:41:07 +0200", "messageId": "", "inReplyTo": "", "references": [""], "textBody": "Hello…", "htmlBody": "

Hello…

", "headers": [ { "Name": "X-Mailer", "Value": "Example" }, { "Name": "X-CM-Raw-Rfc822-Url", "Value": "https://…" } ], "attachments": [ { "name": "invoice.pdf", "contentType": "application/pdf", "inline": false, "content": "JVBERi0xLjQK…" } ] } ``` ## Fields that surprise integrators - `date` is the raw `Date` header, **not** ISO 8601. - `messageId`, `inReplyTo` and `references` are as received (often with angle brackets). Use the `cm-message-id` header for the canonical form. - `to` is the raw `To` header. **`originalRecipient` is the envelope recipient** that matched your domain. Route on this one. - `headers` use PascalCase `Name` and `Value`, unlike the rest of the payload. - Fields the pipeline does not model are not forwarded. ## Attachments Attachment fields: | Field | Description | | - | - | | `name` | File name as sent by the sender. Treat as untrusted. | | `contentType` | Declared media type. | | `inline` | `true` for inline images referenced by `cid:`. | | `contentId` | Content-ID, for matching `cid:` references in `htmlBody`. | | `content` | Base64 file bytes. **Inline mode only.** | | `url` | Download link. **Download-link mode only.** | | `urlExpiresAt` | ISO 8601 expiry of `url`. | There is no `size` field. - **Inline (default).** Each attachment carries `content`. `content` is **omitted** when the file could not be included: it was never stored, was not found, or did not fit the [payload size](#payload-size) budget. The attachment is still listed with its metadata. - **Download links.** Every attachment carries `url` and `urlExpiresAt` instead of `content`, regardless of size, so you never have to branch per attachment. Links expire after the webhook's `presignedUrlExpiryHours` (default 24, at most 168). Download the files before they expire. ## Payload size The whole JSON body is capped at **30 MB**. Inline attachments are base64, so they add about a third to their file size. Attachments are included in order while they fit; those that do not are sent without `content`. If the finished body still exceeds the cap, no webhook call is made for that message. It stays stored and visible in the Email App and is held for replay by CM.com. Use [download links](#attachments) if you expect large attachments. ## Field limits Fields are bounded before delivery. When a field is cut, the message still delivers. | Field | Limit | When exceeded | | - | - | - | | `subject` | 2,000 characters | Truncated | | `fromName` | 500 characters | Truncated | | `from` | 320 characters | Dropped | | `to` | 8,000 characters | Cut at an address boundary | | `cc`, `bcc` | 100 addresses of 320 characters each | Truncated | | `messageId`, `inReplyTo`, each `references` entry | 512 characters | Truncated, keeping the angle brackets | | `references` | 500 entries | Newest 500 kept | | `headers` | 200 entries; names 256 and values 8,000 characters | Extra entries dropped, long text truncated | | attachment `name` | 255 characters | Truncated | | `textBody` | 2 MiB | Dropped; HTML and metadata still deliver | | `htmlBody` | 2 MiB | Dropped; text and metadata still deliver | ## HTML sanitisation `htmlBody` is sanitised once, and the stored copy and the webhook copy are identical. Never render it outside a sandboxed frame on a separate origin with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy. | Aspect | Rule | | - | - | | Tags | Allow-list suited to table-based mail (`a`, `table`, `img`, `div`, `span`, `blockquote`, headings, lists, …). Everything else, including `script`, `style`, `link`, `iframe`, `form` and `svg`, is removed **with its content**. | | Attributes | Allow-list (for example `href`, `src`, `alt`, `style`, `width`, `height`, `align`, `bgcolor`). `class`, `id` and `type` are **kept**, so reply and forward boundaries such as `gmail_quote` or `
` stay detectable. Event handlers such as `onclick` are removed. | | CSS | Property allow-list (colour, border, font, margin, padding, width/height, text, …). At-rules are removed. | | URL schemes | `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`, `cid`. `javascript:`, `vbscript:` and `data:` are removed. | | `cid:` | Kept only if an attachment with that Content-ID exists. | | Remote images | Left intact. | | Control characters | NUL stripped from bodies; NUL, CR and LF stripped from single-line fields (subject, from, headers, …). | --- ## Request Parameters Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/request-parameters.md ## Marketing Email ### Body Parameters | Field | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | from | Address | Yes | Sender's email address and name | | replyTo | Address | No | Reply-to email address and name | | to | Address\[] | Yes | List of primary recipients | | cc | Address\[] | No | List of CC recipients | | bcc | Address\[] | No | List of BCC recipients | | subject | string | Yes | Email subject line | | html | string | Yes (html or text) | HTML email content | | text | string | Yes (html or text) | Plain text email content | | attachments | Attachment\[] | No | List of file attachments | | customerReference | string | No | Your reference for tracking | | inReplyTo | string | No | Message-ID of the email being replied to.
