That reputation directly affects deliverability: how many of your emails land in the inbox versus spam. Email Gateway supports three ways of sourcing that IP: a Shared IP Pool, a Dedicated IP, and Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP). :::info IP allocation isn't yet something you configure yourself. There's currently no option to buy or manage IPs within the UI itself. Provisioning is handled directly by CM.com's Deliverability and Product teams. Self-service IP management is planned. ::: ## Shared IP Pool The Shared IP Pool is the default for every account. Your email sends alongside traffic from other CM.com customers, on infrastructure we actively monitor and keep healthy. There's nothing to set up: if you haven't asked us about IPs before, this is what you're already using. It's the right fit for many senders, especially those with lower or unpredictable volume. Because reputation is shared, we manage the pool proactively rather than leaving it to chance. We track deliverability signals across the pool, monitor for blocklist entries, and step in quickly if a sender's behavior starts to affect the group. Senders who show poor list hygiene or trigger spam complaints are flagged and worked with directly, so the pool stays clean without every customer needing to police it themselves. ## Dedicated IP A dedicated IP is an address used exclusively by your account, allowing you to build your own sending reputation with mailbox providers. It's best suited to senders with consistent, higher volume: a dedicated IP with too little traffic can build reputation more slowly than the shared pool it's replacing. CM.com provisions the IP for you, so you don't need to manage the underlying infrastructure yourself. **Likely a good fit if:** - Your volume is consistent day-over-day - You already have an established sending history - You want your reputation separated from other senders' behavior **Usually not worth it if:** - Your volume is low or unpredictable - You're a brand-new sender with no track record - Your list hygiene or content practices still need work We also offer **Dedicated IP pools**, which group multiple dedicated IPs together under your account. This works well for senders who want to distribute volume across several IPs, for example to separate traffic types or add redundancy, while still keeping full control over their own sending reputation. Pools can also be configured per domain, so different sending domains can each build and maintain their own distinct reputation. ## Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) Bring Your Own IP is available for large senders who own their own IPs and want to leverage their established sending reputation. We support bringing over a /24 CIDR block, a contiguous range of 256 IP addresses, and route your messages through it. This gives you full control over your IP reputation, while reducing the complexity and risk of migrating your infrastructure. It also significantly reduces the need for a traditional warm-up period, since your reputation is already established rather than starting from scratch. This means developers generally don't need to split traffic during warm-up when transferring to a new service: you can move most or all of your traffic over at once instead of gradually ramping up volume. :::info Dedicated IPs, custom pools, and BYOIP aren't available to set up yourself yet. Contact your account manager to request any of these — they'll loop in the product team for the setup. ::: --- ## SMTP Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/smtp.md Email Gateway can send email over SMTP as an alternative to the REST API. This is useful if you're migrating from an existing SMTP setup or working with a tool or library that only speaks SMTP. ## Getting your credentials Your SMTP credentials are available in the Email Gateway App, under Settings > SMTP: - Host: `mx.email.cm.com` - Port: `587` - User: your account's SMTP username, for example `cm-gateway-2d167a9b02` - Password: Your Product Token Each account has its own SMTP username, generated when the account is created. Copy it exactly as shown in Settings > SMTP. It is lowercase and case sensitive. Port `587` is currently the only port we support, using STARTTLS: the connection starts in plaintext and upgrades to TLS before any credentials or message content are sent. ## Verified domains still apply Sending over SMTP doesn't change your domain requirements. The sending domain on each message still needs to be verified under [Domains](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/email-domains), exactly as it does when sending through the REST API. --- ## Suppressions Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/suppressions.md Control which recipients can receive emails from your account. ## Add Manual Suppressions Add suppressions manually with detailed sender and recipient information. ### Request Header ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/suppression/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/manual Content-Type: application/json ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | logicalAccountId | UUID | Yes | The logical account identifier | | Header Name | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | Content-Type | string | Yes | Must be "application/json" | ### Request Body ```json [ { "sender": "marketing@company.com", "recipient": "user@example.com", "unsubscribeType": 1, "emailType": 0 }, { "sender": "newsletter@company.com", "recipient": "customer@domain.com", "unsubscribeType": 1, "emailType": 1 } ] ``` - Maximum 10 suppression requests per API call - All fields are required for each suppression entry #### Response Body **Successful Response (200)** ```json { "success": true, "message": "Success", "status": 200, "data": null } ``` ### Error Responses **Invalid Request - Empty Account ID (400)** ```json { "success": true, "message": "Logical account is empty", "status": 200, "data": null } ``` **Invalid Request - Null Request (400)** ```json { "success": true, "message": "Manual unsubscribe request object is null", "status": 200, "data": null } ``` **Request Limit Exceeded (400)** ```json { "success": false, "message": "Unsubscription requests are restricted to 10 recipients at a time", "status": 400, "data": null } ``` **Server Error (500)** ```json { "success": false, "message": "Failed to unsubscribe from email list", "status": 500, "data": null } ``` --- ## Add Suppression via Unique Key Handle unsubscribes from email unsubscribe links using unique keys. ### Request Header ```http POST https://api.cm.com/email/suppression/v1/{uniqueKey} Content-Type: application/json ``` | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | HardBounce | 1 | Permanent delivery failure | Invalid email addresses, non-existent domains | | SoftBounce | 2 | Temporary delivery failure | Mailbox full, server temporarily unavailable | | RequestedBySystem | 3 | System-initiated suppression | Automated suppressions based on system rules | | RequestedByAdmin | 4 | Admin-initiated suppression | Manual suppressions by administrators | | UnsubscribedByLink | 5 | Unsubscribed via email unsubscribe link | Unique key unsubscribes with reason | | UnsubscribedByHeader | 6 | Unsubscribed via email header action | Unique key unsubscribes without reason | | ManuallyUnsubscribed | 7 | Manually added by user or admin | Manual suppressions via API | ## Email Types The system categorizes emails into different priority levels: | Email Type | Enum Value | Description | Use Cases | | - | - | - | - | | unsubscribeReason | string | No | Optional reason for unsubscribing | ### Suppression List Response Fields | Field | Type | Description | | - | - | - | | id | integer | Unique suppression record ID | | messageRequestId | UUID | Original message request identifier | | sender | string | Email address of the sender | | recipient | string | Email address of the recipient | | createdAt | datetime | When the suppression was created | | modifiedAt | datetime | When the suppression was last modified | | reason | string | Reason for the suppression | | emailType | integer | Email type (0=Market, 1=HighPriority, 2=LowPriority) | | unsubscribeType | integer | Suppression type (1=Manual, 2=Link, 3=Header) | | logicalAccount | UUID | Logical account identifier | ## Example Use Cases ### Marketing Campaign Opt-out ```json [ { "sender": "marketing@company.com", "recipient": "optout-user@example.com", "unsubscribeType": 1, "emailType": 0 } ] ``` ### Email List Hygiene Suppress bounced or invalid email addresses: ```json [ { "sender": "newsletter@company.com", "recipient": "bounced@invalid-domain.com", "unsubscribeType": 1, "emailType": 0 } ] ``` ### Segment-Specific Suppressions Suppress high-priority emails for specific users: ```json [ { "sender": "alerts@company.com", "recipient": "user@example.com", "unsubscribeType": 1, "emailType": 1 } ] ``` ## Search and Filter Suppressions Find all marketing suppressions for a specific domain: ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/suppression/v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/subscriptions?searchEmail=@example.com&emailType=0&pageSize=50 ``` ## Pagination for Large Lists Retrieve suppressions in manageable chunks: ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/suppression/v1/accounts/50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b/subscriptions?pageSize=25&pageNumber=3 ``` ## Rate Limits and Constraints - **Manual Suppressions**: Maximum 10 suppressions per request - **Pagination**: Maximum 100 results per page - **Search**: Email search supports partial matching ## Troubleshooting 1. **Suppression Not Working**: Verify logical account ID and email format 2. **Search Not Finding Results**: Verify search terms and email type filters 3. **Unique Key Invalid**: Ensure unique key is valid and not expired 4. **Batch Limit Exceeded**: Split large suppression lists into batches of 10 or few --- ## Test Your Integration Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/test-your-integration.md We understand the importance of testing your integration in a secure and controlled environment. That’s why we offer two testing options: **Sandbox Mode** and **Integration Mode**. These features allow you to validate your workflow and test your integration without impacting real users or your domain reputation. Below, we’ll guide you through each mode and how to use them effectively. :::info Both the **Transactional Email API** and the **Marketing Email API** offer Sandbox and Integration mode, providing a safe and controlled environment for testing your integration. ::: ## Sandbox Mode Sandbox Mode is designed for validating the integrity of your email requests without sending any emails. This mode ensures that your request meets service requirements before it’s processed for delivery. When Sandbox Mode is enabled, our system performs the following checks: - **Data Validation:** Ensures all required fields are present and correctly formatted. - **Email Size Verification:** Confirms that the email size is within acceptable limits. - **Attachment Validation:** Checks that attachments meet our requirements. - **Message Format Compliance:** Validates the structure of your email content. To enable Sandbox Mode, include the header `"Sandbox-Mode: true"` in your API request. When enabled, our service validates your request without delivering messages to recipients. Default value for `Sandbox-Mode` header is false. ### Example Request Here’s an example of a request in Sandbox Mode: ```json curl -X POST "https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/marketing" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: your-product-token" \ -H "Sandbox-Mode: true" \ -d '{ "from": { "email": "sender@example.com", "name": "Sender Name" }, "replyTo": { "email": "reply@example.com", "name": "Reply Name" }, "to": [ { "email": "recipient@example.com", "name": "Recipient Name" } ], "cc": [ { "email": "cc@example.com", "name": "CC Name" } ], "bcc": [ { "email": "bcc@example.com", "name": "BCC Name" } ], "subject": "Sandbox mode example", "html": "

This is an example request for sandbox mode

", "text": "This is an example request for sandbox mode", "attachments": [ { "fileName": "document.pdf", "content": "base64-encoded-content", "contentType": "application/pdf", "contentId": "attachment-id" } ], "customerReference": "your-reference" } ``` ```yaml from: email: "sender@example.com" name: "Sender Name" replyTo: email: "reply@example.com" name: "Reply Name" to: - email: "recipient@example.com" name: "Recipient Name" cc: - email: "cc@example.com" name: "CC Name" bcc: - email: "bcc@example.com" name: "BCC Name" subject: "Sandbox mode example" html: "

This is an example request for sandbox mode

" text: "This is an example request for sandbox mode" attachments: - fileName: "document.pdf" content: "base64-encoded-content" contentType: "application/pdf" contentId: "attachment-id" customerReference: "your-reference" ``` ### Response A valid request will return a `200 OK` response, indicating that your email meets all validation requirements. ```json { "status": 200, "message": "Sandbox mode is enabled. The message is accepted but will not be sent.", "success": true, "messageId": "df9990e2-f7cb-450d-9528-6e6698c8abab" } ``` ```yaml status: 200 message: "Sandbox mode is enabled. The message is accepted but will not be sent." success: true messageId: "df9990e2-f7cb-450d-9528-6e6698c8abab" ``` **Note:** This differs from the `202 Accepted` response returned for live email requests. If you submit a request with sandbox mode enabled, but your request body is invalid, you will receive one or more error messages with error codes. ## Important Notes - Messages sent in Sandbox Mode do not contribute to your monthly usage limit. - No logs are generated for requests with Sandbox Mode enabled. - This feature is intended for testing and validating your requests. ## Integration Mode Integration Mode lets you test the entire integration of your system with our Email Gateway. This setup provides a safe and reliable way to test your integrations and workflows without affecting real users or risking your domain reputation. By using this test domain, you can confidently fine-tune your processes while ensuring no unintended impact on your audience. When you send an email to a recipient using the domain `@sink.cm.com`, our Mail Transfer Agent (MTA) will accept the message but automatically drop it. This means the email will not be delivered to any recipient's mailbox. All other processes will work the same while using Integration Mode. :::danger Please note that any messages you send to `@sink.cm.com` will contribute to your monthly usage limit. If you’re on a pay-as-you-go plan, these messages will be counted as billable usage. ::: ### Example Request Here’s an example of a request in Integration Mode: ```json curl -X POST "https://api.cm.com/email/gateway/v1/marketing" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-CM-PRODUCTTOKEN: your-product-token" \ -H "Sandbox-Mode: true" \ -d '{ "from": { "email": "promotions@example.com", "name": "Example Promotions" }, "replyTo": { "email": "support@example.com", "name": "Example Promotions Support" }, "to": [ { "email": "customer1@sink.cm.com", "name": "Customer One" }, { "email": "customer2@sink.cm.com", "name": "Customer Two" } ], "cc": [ { "email": "customer3@sink.cm.com", "name": "Customer Three" } ], "subject": "Flash Sale - 50% Off Everything!", "html": "

Flash Sale Alert!

Everything in our store is 50% off for the next 24 hours!

Use code: FLASH50

", "text": "Flash Sale Alert! Everything in our store is 50% off for the next 24 hours! Use code: FLASH50", "customerReference": "flash-sale-march-2024" } ``` ```yaml from: email: "promotions@example.com" name: "Example Promotions" replyTo: email: "support@example.com" name: "Example Promotions Support" to: - email: "customer1@sink.cm.com" name: "Customer One" - email: "customer2@sink.cm.com" name: "Customer Two" cc: - email: "customer3@sink.cm.com" name: "Customer Three" subject: "Flash Sale - 50% Off Everything!" html: "

For example, a successful request will return a `202 OK`. However, please note that while this indicates the message was sent successfully, it is not actually sent. ```json { "status": 202, "message": "Accepted", "success": true, "messageId": "5dcdf71f-96d6-4763-8d70-ef17d8aa6dbc" } ``` ```yaml status: 202 message: "Accepted" success: true messageId: "5dcdf71f-96d6-4763-8d70-ef17d8aa6dbc" ``` For all response codes see the [response codes](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/response-codes) page. ## Important Notes When you send an email to a recipient with the domain sink.cm.com (e.g., [customer1@sink.cm.com](mailto\:customer1@sink.cm.com)): - Our system processes the email, but ensures it is not delivered by dropping it at the Mail Transfer Agent (MTA). - These emails still count toward your total sent emails, as they are using the whole infrastructure. - In your email logs, these messages will have a status labeled as `Integration`, making it easy to distinguish emails sent in integration mode from regular ones. --- ## Usage Alerts Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/usage-alerts.md Manage alerts to monitor your accounts usage. The Email Alerts API enables you to configure and manage usage alerts for your account. You can create up to 8 alerts per account to monitor your accounts usage and receive notifications when thresholds are reached. :::info This feature is currently unavailable to pay-as-you-go users. ::: ## List Alerts Retrieve all alerts configured for a logical account. #### Request Header ```http GET https://api.cm.com/email/alerts/v1/account/{logicalAccount}/alerts/list ``` ### Response Body **Successful Response (200)** ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Alerts found.", "data": [ { "id": 5, "logicalAccountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "alertName": "alert 2", "metric": "Usage", "threshold": "<80", "recipient": "wemixe7699@amcret.com", "createdDate": "2025-08-25T05:14:02.069378", "updatedDate": "2025-08-25T05:14:02.069378" }, { "id": 4, "logicalAccountId": "50025f6a-d4fd-4a23-9e2e-bbee1cf67d2b", "alertName": "alert 1", "metric": "Usage", "threshold": ">90", "recipient": "testok@xyz.com", "createdDate": "2025-08-25T05:13:26.014882", "updatedDate": "2025-08-25T05:13:26.014882" } ] } ``` ## Delete Alert Delete an existing alert. ### Request Header ```http DELETE https://api.cm.com/email/alerts/v1/account/{logicalAccount}/alerts/delete/{id} ``` ### Response Body **Successful Response (200)** ```json { "success": true, "status": 200, "message": "Successfully deleted email alert with id 14", "data": 1 } ``` ### Error Responses **Alert Not Found (400)** ```json { "success": false, "status": 400, "message": "Alert not found or already deleted.", "data": -1 } ``` **Internal Error (500)** ```json { "status": 500, "message": "An unexpected internal server error occurred.", "success": false, "data": null } ``` ## Request Parameters ### Path Parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | Logical Account | GUID | Yes | Unique identifier for the logical account | | id | int32 | Yes | Alert ID (for update/delete operations only) | ### Request Body Fields | Field | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | Alert Name | string | Yes | Name of the alert | | metric | string | Yes | Usage | | threshold | string | Yes | Threshold with operator (e.g., ">90", "\<50", "=75") | | recipient | string | Yes | Email addresses (comma-separated for multiple) | ## Threshold Operators | Operator | Symbol | Description | | - | - | - | | Over | > | Alert when metric is above threshold | | Below | \< | Alert when metric is below threshold | | Equal | = | Alert when metric equals threshold | ## Best Practices 1. **Alert Limit**: Remember the 8-alert limit per account. This may be due to misconfigured mail servers or network issues. | | Protocol Errors | Delivery failed: A protocol error occurred during communication with the recipient's mail server. Please ensure your message meets all technical requirements. | | Authentication Failed | Delivery failed: Sender authentication was unsuccessful. Please check your sending domain's SPF, DKIM, or DMARC settings and try again. | | Temporary Rejection | Delivery delayed: The recipient's server temporarily rejected the message. Our system will attempt to resend your email automatically. | | Delayed | Delivery delayed: Your message could not be delivered immediately and will be retried. Webhook Verification Source: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/webhooks/webhook-verification.md Verify every webhook before you process it. Verification confirms that the request came from the CM.com Email Gateway and that the body was not altered. Without it, your application cannot tell a real event from a forged one. The timestamp check limits how long a captured request stays valid. It does not stop an exact copy of a valid request from being accepted again inside that window. See [Replay protection and duplicate events](#replay-protection-and-duplicate-events). ## Headers Each signed webhook carries three headers: | Header | Description | | - | - | | `svix-id` | The ID of the email message (a UUID). Every event for the same message, such as sent, delivered and bounced, carries the same `svix-id`. **Do not use it to deduplicate.** Use `data.id` from the payload. | | `svix-timestamp` | Unix time in **milliseconds** (Svix proper uses seconds). | | `svix-signature` | Base64 HMAC-SHA512, no `v1,` prefix. | ## Prerequisites - Your **Webhook Secret**, found under **Settings → Integration** in the Email App. - A publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint that accepts `POST` requests. - Access to the **raw, unparsed request body**. Re-serialised JSON produces a signature mismatch. ## Verification steps 1. Check that `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp` and `svix-signature` are all present. 2. Check that `svix-timestamp` is within your tolerance window (we recommend 5 minutes). This rejects old requests. It does not reject an exact copy of a recent one. 3. Compute the signature and compare it with `svix-signature` using a constant-time comparison. ```text signature = base64( HMAC_SHA512( key = UTF8(secret), data = svix-id + "." + svix-timestamp + "." + rawBodyBytes ) ) ``` - The key is your Webhook Secret used as raw UTF-8. Do not base64-decode it or strip a `whsec_` prefix. - Sign the **exact bytes** received. - A stock Svix library rejects these signatures because of the millisecond timestamp. Use the SDKs below or the example in this page. ```js const crypto = require('crypto'); const TOLERANCE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; function verify(secret, headers, rawBody /* Buffer */) { const id = headers['svix-id']; const ts = headers['svix-timestamp']; const sig = headers['svix-signature']; if (!id || !ts || !sig) return false; if (!(Math.abs(Date.now() - Number(ts)) <= TOLERANCE_MS)) return false; const mac = crypto.createHmac('sha512', secret) .update(`${id}.${ts}.`) .update(rawBody) .digest('base64'); const got = Buffer.from(sig); const want = Buffer.from(mac); return got.length === want.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(got, want); } ``` ## SDKs Official SDKs handle header checks, timestamp validation and signature comparison. The tolerance window is configurable when you create the validator. | Language | Package | | - | - | | .NET | `CM.Email.WebhookVerification` | | Python | `cm-email-webhook-verification` | | Rust | `cm-email-webhook-verification` | ## Replay protection and duplicate events The signature covers `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp` and the raw body, so nobody without your Webhook Secret can change a webhook or give it a newer timestamp. An exact copy of a valid webhook can still be accepted again until it falls outside your tolerance window. Delivery is also at-least-once, so the same event can arrive more than once, for example when we retry a delivery. Make your handler idempotent by storing the `data.id` of every event you process and skipping repeats: - `data.id` is unique per event and stays the same when we retry that event. - `svix-id` is the email message ID, shared by all events for that message. Skipping on it would drop real events. - Events can arrive out of order. Compare `createdAt` before an older event overwrites newer state. ```js // Use a shared store in production, for example a database unique key or Redis SET NX const processedEventIds = new Set(); function handle(event) { if (processedEventIds.has(event.data.id)) return; // already handled, still respond 2xx processedEventIds.add(event.data.id); // Process the event } ``` Call this only after the request has passed verification. ## Respond - On success, return a `2xx` status. Do slow work asynchronously. - On failure, return `401`. Do not reveal why verification failed in the response. ## Failure types | Failure | Cause | | - | - | | Missing headers | One or more of the three headers is absent. | | Invalid timestamp | `svix-timestamp` is not a valid number. | | Expired timestamp | `svix-timestamp` is outside the tolerance window. | | Invalid signature | The computed signature does not match `svix-signature`. | ## Best practices - Verify before you process anything. - Keep the secret out of source control. Rotate it if it leaks. - Handle duplicates. Store the `data.id` of processed events, not `svix-id`, and skip repeats. Delivery is at-least-once. See [Replay protection and duplicate events](#replay-protection-and-duplicate-events). - Keep server clocks synced with NTP. Clock drift is a common cause of expired timestamps. ## Troubleshooting **Invalid signature** - Wrong secret. - Body modified before verification, for example by framework parsing or a proxy. Verify against the raw bytes. - A proxy altered the headers. **Expired timestamp** - Clock drift on your server. - Slow queue processing between receipt and verification. Verify on receipt, then queue. - Replaying a captured request during testing. Inbound email webhooks use the same scheme. See [Verify and Delivery](https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/guides/receiving-emails/verify-and-delivery). --- ## Email Gateway API API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/email-gateway-api/v1/api-reference Base URL: `https://api.cm.com` ### POST /email/gateway/v1/marketing Send marketing email Sends a marketing email, such as a newsletter or promotion. An unsubscribe link and a one-click unsubscribe header are added automatically. Set `scheduledAt` to deliver the email later, up to 72 hours ahead. The response contains a `messageId`; delivery results are available through webhooks and in the email logs. ### POST /email/gateway/v1/transactional Send transactional email Sends a transactional email, such as a password reset, order confirmation or one-time code. Use the `priority` query parameter to mark time-sensitive emails as `high`. Set `scheduledAt` to deliver the email later, up to 72 hours ahead. The response contains a `messageId`; delivery results are available through webhooks and in the email logs. ### POST /email/configuration/v1/configuration/add-domain Add domain Registers a domain for sending. DNS records are generated for the domain; add them to your DNS provider and then verify the domain. Use the get domain endpoint to retrieve the records. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains List account domains Returns all domains registered for an account, including their DNS records, verification status and tracking settings. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domainId} Get domain Returns the DNS records you must configure for a domain, and whether each record is currently valid. ### DELETE /email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domainId} Delete domain Removes a domain and all of its DNS records from the account. ### PUT /email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domain}/sending Enable or disable sending Enables or disables sending for a domain. The response contains the domain configuration after the change. ### PUT /email/configuration/v1/configuration/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/domains/{domain}/receiving Enable or disable receiving Enables or disables receiving for a domain. Receiving requires the MX record of the domain to be verified. The response contains the domain configuration after the change. ### POST /email/configuration/v1/dns/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/verify Verify DNS records Checks the DNS records of a domain against the records that were generated for it and reports whether each record is valid. A domain is ready to send once all of its records are valid. DNS changes can take from a few minutes up to 48 hours to propagate, so run the verification again if records are still reported as invalid. ### POST /email/configuration/v1/dns/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/verify/{capability} Verify DNS capability Checks the DNS records of a domain for one capability only: `sending` (the CNAME records), `receiving` (the MX record) or `all`. A record is valid when it is found in DNS with the expected value. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/emails/receiving List received emails Returns a page of the emails received on your receiving domains. Filter by time range, direction or search text. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/emails/receiving/{emailId} Get received email Returns the details of one received email, including its headers, body and attachment metadata. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/emails/receiving/{emailId}/attachments List received email attachments Returns the attachments of a received email, including a download URL for each attachment. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccount}/inbound-webhook List receiving webhooks Returns the receiving webhooks of an account. A receiving webhook is called for each email received on a domain. ### POST /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccount}/inbound-webhook Create receiving webhook Creates a receiving webhook that is called for each email received on a domain. The webhook URL must be an HTTPS URL on port 443. ### PATCH /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccount}/inbound-webhook Update receiving webhook Updates a receiving webhook. Only the fields you provide are changed. ### DELETE /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccount}/inbound-webhook/{id} Delete receiving webhook Deletes a receiving webhook. The response contains the number of deleted rows. ### POST /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/create Create webhook Registers a webhook URL for an email event type, such as `delivered` or `bounced`. Use the type `global` to receive all events on one URL. Registering a type that already has a webhook replaces its URL. The response contains the ID of the webhook. ### GET /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/list List webhooks Returns the webhook configuration of an account. ### DELETE /email/configuration/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/delete Delete webhook Deletes the webhook that is registered for an email event type. ### POST /email/suppression/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/manual Add manual suppression Adds recipients to the suppression list, so that emails of the given type are no longer sent to them. A request can contain up to 10 entries. ### POST /email/suppression/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/subscriptions Search unsubscribes Searches the unsubscribe list with a set of filters in the request body. Results are paginated. ### GET /email/suppression/v1/accounts/{logicalAccountId}/subscriptions List suppressions Returns the suppression list of an account. Filter by recipient email address and email type. Results are paginated, with up to 100 results per page. ### POST /email/suppression/v1/{uniqueKey} Update suppression Unsubscribes a recipient using the unique key from the unsubscribe link in an email. You can optionally provide the reason the recipient gives for unsubscribing. --- ## Changelog Live on production: v1.4.0 (released 4 Nov 2026). See [Data retention](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md). - Logs are written once and cannot be changed. - To view or export them, see [View access and change logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md). ## Related - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) --- ## Governance Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance.md Centralized access management platform controlling who can access what resources under which conditions. ## Explore --- ## Access Management Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/access-management.md In the Governance portal you give users and teams roles. Each role lets them do certain things, in one account or across your whole organization, on all resources or only some. ## What you can do | Task | What it means | | - | - | | **Manage role assignments** | Give a user or team a role, change it or remove it, in an account or the whole organization, on specific resources. Everything else in Governance builds on this. | | **Invite users** | Bring people into your organization. Pending invitations are tracked until accepted. | | **Manage teams** | Group users so one assignment covers everyone. | | **Create custom roles** | Build roles from the permissions that fit your organization. | | **Review logs** | See who accessed what, and who changed what. | ## The building blocks 1. A [principal](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) is who gets access. 2. A [role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) is what they can do. 3. A [resource](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md) is what they can do it on. 4. A [scope](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md) is where it applies. 5. A [role assignment](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) ties these together. ## Related - [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md) - [Custom roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Access Logs Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs/access-logs.md The access log records each access decision Governance makes: who asked, what for, and whether it was allowed or denied. ## What each entry shows | Field | Meaning | | - | - | | Time | When the decision was made. | | Principal | The user, team or token that asked. | | Application | The application the request was for. | | Permission | What was requested. Shown without its namespace prefix. | | Decision | Allowed or denied. | ## Use it to - See who asked for what, and whether it was allowed or denied. To understand a decision, see [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md). ## Good to know - You need the Governance **Editor** permission to view it. - Entries are kept for 3 months. See [Data retention](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md). ## Related - [View access and change logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md) - [Change logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs/change-logs.md) --- ## Change Logs Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs/change-logs.md The change log records each change made to access settings in Governance: who made it, what it was, and how it looked before and after. ## What each entry shows | Field | Meaning | | - | - | | Time | When the change happened. | | Actor | Who made the change. | | Type | What kind of thing changed (see below). | | Action | Create, update or delete. | | Target | The name of what changed. | | Before and after | The previous and current state. | ## What is recorded | Type | Recorded when | | - | - | | Role assignment | A role is assigned, changed or removed. | | Team | A team is changed. | | Team member | A team's members change. | | Custom role | A custom role is created or changed. Adding or removing permissions counts as an update of the whole role. | | Invitation | An invitation is created or changed. | | Onboarding | An organization is onboarded. | ## Use it to - See who changed access settings, and when. - Compare the state before and after a change. ## Good to know - You need the Governance **Editor** permission to view it. - Names are looked up when you view the log. If a person or application has since been deleted, its name is empty. - Entries are kept for 3 months. See [Data retention](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md). ## Related - [View access and change logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md) - [Access logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs/access-logs.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) --- ## Accounts and Organizations Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md Access in Governance always applies within a **scope**. There are two scopes: - **Organization**: your company as a whole. - **Account**: one workspace inside your organization. One organization owns one or more accounts. ## Choosing a scope | Assigned at | Applies to | | - | - | | **Account** | That account only. | | **Organization** | Every account in the organization. | Most roles are assigned at account level. Only the **Platform Owner** role is normally assigned at organization level. ## How the two scopes combine When Governance checks access in an account, it looks at the grants made on that account **and** the grants made on its organization. Both count. The reverse is not true. A check at organization level looks at organization grants only, so an account-level grant never gives access to the whole organization. ## Common mistake An organization-level assignment is not limited to one account. If someone should only work in one account, assign their role at that account. ## Related - [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Custom Roles Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md A **custom role** is a role your organization creates itself, by choosing which [permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) it includes. ## When to use one Use a custom role when the roles that come with Governance give too much, or too little, for a group of people. For example, a role that can view and edit agents but cannot manage users. ## Rules - A custom role belongs to your organization and can't be used by others. - The name must be unique within your organization. - It can only include permissions that exist. - Creating or changing one needs the Governance Editor permission. - Changes to a custom role's permissions are recorded in the change log. ## After you create it A custom role does nothing until you assign it. Assign it to a user or a [team](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md) like any other role. See [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). ## Related - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) --- ## Permissions Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md A **permission** is one specific action someone is allowed to do, such as reading data, changing a configuration or managing users. ## Who defines them Permissions are owned by the application teams. The application defines its own permissions. Governance only stores them and checks them. You cannot change what an application's permissions mean. ## How they are named A permission name has two parts, joined by a dot: the application's **namespace** and the permission name. ```text Namespace.Name ``` For example, `Governance.Editor`. Each application owns its own namespace, so two applications can use the same permission name without clashing. ## Permissions and roles A permission can't be assigned directly to a user. It can only be given through a [role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md): permissions are grouped into roles, and you assign the role. | Concept | Answers | | - | - | | **Permission** | What can be done? | | **Role** | How are permissions grouped? | | **Resource** | On what? | ## Related - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md) - [Custom roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md) --- ## Principals Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md A **principal** is anyone or anything that can be given access. When Governance decides whether to allow an action, the first question is always: _who is asking?_ ## Types of principal | Type | What it is | How it is identified | | - | - | - | | **User** | A person with a CM.com account. | Their CM.com user GUID. | | **Team** | A group of users that share the same access. | An ID Governance creates when the team is made in the Governance portal. | | **Product token** | A machine identity for a system or integration, not a person. | The ID of an existing CM.com API key. Governance registers the key; it does not create one. | ## Good to know - **CM.com Platform is the source of truth for users.** Governance copies user details from Platform, so you do not create users in Governance. - **Access can be given to a user directly, or through a team.** A user gets everything their teams are given. See [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md). - **A principal has no access on its own.** It gets access only through a [role assignment](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). ## Related - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Accounts and organizations](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Resources Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md A **resource** is the thing being accessed, such as a profile, an agent or a record inside an application. Governance checks access on the resource itself, not just on the application. Each application defines its own resources. Governance does not decide what they are. ## What a resource looks like A resource is a path, like a web address: ```text /resource/5/items/10 ``` ## Patterns When you assign a role, you say _which resources_ it covers by writing a pattern. | Pattern | Covers | | - | - | | `/resource/5/items/10` | Exactly that resource. | | `/resource/5/items/{id}` | Any single item under `/resource/5/items/`. `{id}` stands for one path segment. | | `/resource/5/*` | Everything under `/resource/5/`, at any depth. | | `*` or left blank | Every resource. | Matching ignores upper and lower case, and ignores anything after a `?` in the address. ## Good to know - **A blank resource means everything.** Leaving the field empty gives the role on all resources, not none. - **Patterns are not checked for typos.** A wrong pattern is accepted and simply matches nothing, so the person gets no access. Check the path after you assign. - **Applications can list their resources for you.** If an application supports it, you can pick resources from a list instead of typing a pattern. ## Related - [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Role Assignments Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md A **role assignment** is what actually gives someone access. It connects four things: | Part | Meaning | | - | - | | **Principal** | Who gets the access: a user, a team or a product token. | | **Role** | What they can do. | | **Scope** | Where it applies: one account, or the whole organization. | | **Resource** | Which resources it covers. Blank means all. | For example: _the Support team_ gets _a read-only role_ in _the Sales account_ on _`/agents/*`_. ## How assignments are combined Assignments only add access. A person's access is everything they are given directly, plus everything their teams are given. There is no assignment that takes access away. ## Changing and removing - You cannot edit the principal or the scope of an assignment. To move it, remove it and create a new one. - Removing an assignment deletes it. Every change is recorded in the change log. - The same combination of principal, role, scope and resource can exist only once. ## Related - [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Accounts and organizations](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md) - [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Roles Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md A **role** is a named bundle of [permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md), for example "Support" or "Administrator". Instead of giving someone many permissions one by one, you give them a role. ## Kinds of role | Kind | Defined by | Used for | | - | - | - | | **App role** | The application's team | Responsibilities specific to one application. | | **Global role** | CM.com | Broad roles not tied to one application, such as Administrator, User and Platform Owner. | | **Custom role** | Your organization | Your own mix of permissions. See [Custom roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md). | Roles are not the same in every application. An application decides which roles it offers. ## How roles are used A role does nothing until it is given to a [principal](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) or a [team](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md) in a [scope](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md). That is a [role assignment](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). ## Related - [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) - [Custom roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md) --- ## Teams Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md A **team** is a group of users. Give a role to the team once, and every member gets it. ## Why use a team - **Less work.** Assign a role to "Support" instead of to each person. - **Easy changes.** Add someone to the team to give them access. Remove them to take it away. ## How teams work - Teams belong to an organization and are created in the Governance portal. - A team can receive role assignments, like a user. - A member gets all the access the team is given, on top of any access they have directly. - When a member is removed from a team, they lose the access they got through it. Access given to them directly stays. ## Example An organization creates a team called **Integration Specialists** and assigns it a role that allows configuring agents. Anyone added to the team can configure agents. When a specialist leaves the team, they can't. ## Related - [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) --- ## Assign a Role Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/assign-a-role.md Assigning a role gives a user or a team the permissions in that role. You do it in the User Management view of the Governance portal. You need the Governance **Editor** permission on the account. ## Steps 1. Open **User Management** and select the user or team. 2. Choose the **role**. 3. Choose the **scope**: one account, or the whole organization. 4. Optional: enter a **resource** to limit the role to specific resources. Leave it blank for all resources. If you enter one, also choose the application it belongs to. 5. Save. | Field | What to enter | | - | - | | Principal | The user or team that gets the role. | | Role | What they can do. | | Scope | Where it applies: an account or the organization. | | Resource | What they can do it on. Blank means all. | ## Change several assignments at once One save can add, change and remove assignments together. Each change is processed on its own. If some fail, the rest still go through, and you see how many succeeded and which ones failed. ## Good to know - Assigning a role the person already has changes nothing. - You can't change the user, team or scope of an existing assignment. Delete it and create a new one. - Removing an assignment deletes it. - Every change appears in the [change log](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md). ## Related - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md) - [Create a team](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/create-a-team.md) --- ## Create a Custom Role Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/create-a-custom-role.md A custom role is a role you build for your organization from existing permissions. Use it when the ready-made roles give too much or too little access. You create custom roles in the **Custom roles** section of the Governance portal. You need the Governance **Editor** permission on the organization. ## Steps 1. Open **Custom roles** and create a new role. 2. Enter a **name**. 3. Choose the **permissions** the role should include. 4. Save. ## Rules - The name must be unique in your organization. - Every permission you choose must exist. You can only pick permissions that applications have defined. - The organization must be active. ## Use the role Once saved, you can [assign the role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/assign-a-role.md) to users and teams like any other role. ## Good to know - Adding or removing permissions later updates the role as a whole. - Creating and changing custom roles is recorded in the [change log](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md). ## Related - [Custom roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/custom-roles.md) - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) - [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) --- ## Create a Team Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/create-a-team.md A team groups users so you can assign a role once and it applies to everyone in the team. You manage teams in the **Teams** view of the Governance portal. You need the Governance **Editor** permission. ## Steps 1. Open **Teams** and create a new team. 2. Enter a **team name**. 3. Add **members**. Only users can be members. 4. Save. The team can now be given roles like any other user. See [Assign a role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/assign-a-role.md). ## Change a team You can rename a team and add or remove members. Make at least one change before saving. ## Good to know - Members get every role assigned to the team. - Changes to a team appear in the [change log](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md). ## Related - [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) --- ## Invite a User Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/invite-a-user.md Invite people from the **Pending Invitations** tab in the User Management view of the Governance portal. You choose the roles up front, so they have access as soon as they accept. You need the Governance **Editor** permission on the account. ## Steps 1. Open **User Management**, then the **Pending Invitations** tab. 2. Choose the type of access: - **Platform:** a CM.com Platform role, sent to Platform directly. - **Resource-based:** roles on specific resources, handled by Governance. 3. Enter the **email address** of each person. Use one email per person. 4. Choose the **scope**: an account or the whole organization. 5. Choose the **roles**. For resource-based access, also choose the application and resource. 6. Send the invitation. The Platform option only appears for users with Governance admin rights. ## What happens next - Each email is handled on its own. If one fails, the others still go through. - The invitation shows in **Pending Invitations**, with its roles and expiry. - When the person accepts and their CM.com account is matched by email, the pending roles become real [role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). ## Cancel an invitation Revoke it from **Pending Invitations**. This removes the invitation and all its roles at once. ## Related - [Assign a role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/assign-a-role.md) - [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) - [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) --- ## Onboarding an Organization Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/onboarding-an-organization.md Onboarding copies your organization from CM.com Platform into Governance. Until it is done, you can't use the Governance portal for that organization. ## What gets copied | From CM.com Platform | Becomes in Governance | | - | - | | The organization's accounts | Accounts | | Users and their organization membership | Users | | Users' role assignments | An equivalent role assignment for each | ## Start onboarding 1. Open any account in the Governance portal. If the organization is not onboarded yet, you are sent to the onboarding page. 2. Start onboarding. It runs in the background, so you can leave the page. 3. Wait until the status shows **Completed**. Only Platform Owners can initiate onboarding ## Statuses | Status | Meaning | | - | - | | Not started | Onboarding has not been run. | | In progress | The copy is running. | | Completed | Done. The portal is available. | | Failed | Something went wrong. | The portal stays blocked until the status is **Completed**. ## Good to know - Onboarding copies existing access. It does not create users or log anyone in. See [What Governance does not do](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-governance-does-not-do.md). ## Related - [Accounts and organizations](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md) - [Invite a user](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/invite-a-user.md) - [Assign a role](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/assign-a-role.md) --- ## View Access and Change Logs Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/customers/view-logs.md Governance keeps two logs: - **Access log:** who tried to do what, and whether it was allowed. - **Change log:** who changed access settings, and what changed. You can view both in the Governance portal. You need the Governance **Editor** permission. ## Use the logs 1. Open the access log or the change log. 2. Choose a **time range**. 3. Page through the results. You can show 1 to 100 rows per page. The default is 50. 4. To keep a copy, export the results to CSV. Logs are kept for 3 months. See [Data retention](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md). ## Access log | Column | Shows | | - | - | | Time | When the check happened. | | Principal | The user, team or token that asked. | | Application | The application involved. | | Permission | What was requested. | | Decision | Whether it was allowed or denied. | ## Change log | Column | Shows | | - | - | | Time | When the change happened. | | Actor | Who made it. | | Type | What was changed: a role assignment, team, team member, custom role, invitation or onboarding. | | Action | Create, update or delete. | | Target | The name of what changed. | | Before and after | The previous and current state. | ## Related - [Data retention](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Data Retention & Deletion Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/data-retention.md Governance keeps two kinds of log: access logs (who accessed what) and change logs (who changed what). ## How long logs are kept | Log | Kept for | | - | - | | Access logs | 3 months | | Change logs | 3 months | After 3 months, the logs are deleted automatically. You don't need to request it. ## How logs are stored Logs are stored in a data lake as **write once, read many** files. Once a log is written it cannot be changed. It can only be read until it is deleted. ## What this means for you - You can review activity from the last 3 months. - To keep a record for longer, save the logs you need before they are deleted. --- ## FAQ Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/faq.md ## What is Governance? Governance decides who can access what. It supports access based on roles and resources, groups users into teams, and records access logs and change logs. Customers can create their own custom roles. See [What is Governance?](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-is-governance.md). ## Is Governance replacing the current authorization? Yes, in stages rather than all at once. - **Phase 1:** Governance replaces the existing authorization with the Governance API. - **Phase 2:** The Governance UI replaces user management. ## Will callers notice a difference? No. The response callers get keeps the same shape. What changes is which system works out the decision. ## Do all organizations and applications move at the same time? No. Organizations and applications are onboarded one by one, and each can switch independently. ## Do application teams have to use Governance? No. They can keep using platform roles, and need to do nothing. Governance is for teams that want finer control through application-specific roles or resources. ## How does an application team get started? 1. Your team lead is added to the Governance portal to manage the application's roles. 2. If you want access by resource, build an endpoint that lists your resources. 3. Use the libraries Governance provides to check access. ## Does an application have to provide resources? No. Without a resource endpoint, no resources are listed for that application. Customers can still assign roles without a resource. ## Why am I redirected from user management to Governance? CM.com does not want several screens for managing users. If you don't need Governance features, you can keep assigning platform roles on the Governance screens as before. ## Related - [What Governance does not do](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-governance-does-not-do.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## Getting Started Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/getting-started.md Start here to set up access for your organization. - New to Governance? Read [What is Governance?](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-is-governance.md) and [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md). - Setting up access for your organization? See the **For Customers** guides in the sidebar. --- ## How Access Decisions Work Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md When someone uses an application, the application asks Governance whether they may do what they are trying to do. Governance answers **Allow** or **Deny**, and the application acts on the answer. \[How an access check works: an access request is checked for Governance management; if managed, permissions are collected and the request is allowed or denied, otherwise Platform answers] ## The steps 1. **Is the scope an account or an organization?** Governance decides requests at these two scopes only. A request at any other scope goes to Platform. 2. **Is that account or organization using Governance?** If not, the request goes to Platform. 3. **Is the person known to Governance?** If not, the request goes to Platform. 4. **Governance collects the person's permissions.** It looks at the roles given to the person and to the teams they belong to. For an account, that includes roles given on its organization. See [Accounts and organizations](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/accounts-and-organizations.md). 5. **Governance applies the resource.** A role given on a specific resource only counts for that resource. A role given with no resource counts for all of them. See [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md). 6. **Governance decides.** The request is allowed only if the person has every permission the application asked about. Otherwise it is denied. Whenever a request goes to Platform, Platform's response comes back through Governance, which passes it on to the application. ## What Governance needs to know | It looks at | Meaning | | - | - | | **The person** | Who is making the request. | | **The scope** | Where they are working: an account or an organization. | | **The resource** | What they want to use. Optional. | | **The permissions** | What they want to do. | ## Good to know - Roles only add access. Nothing takes access away, so a person with no matching permission is denied. See [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). - Permissions reach a person only through roles, either given to them directly or through a team. See [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) and [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md). - Governance keeps access logs. See [Audit logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs.md). ## Related - [What is Governance?](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-is-governance.md) - [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md) - [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md) --- ## Scenario: Halo Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/scenarios-halo.md Halo contains profiles and agents. Not everyone in an organization needs the same level of access to them. This example shows how Governance handles that. ## The goal | Group | Should be able to | | - | - | | **Integration Specialists** | Configure specific agents. | | **Support** | View how agents behave. | | **Developers** | Manage everything. | ## The setup 1. **Create a team for each group.** See [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md). 2. **Add users to the teams.** 3. **Assign a role to each team on the resources it needs.** A resource can be a whole profile, or one agent in it, such as the Weather Agent in Hugo's profile. See [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md). 4. **Give individual access only where needed.** A single person can also be assigned a role directly, outside any team. ## What happens next When someone uses Halo, Governance checks their access: - A Support user who tries to configure the Weather Agent is **denied**. - An Integration Specialist who configures it is **allowed**. - A user added to the Developers team can manage everything straight away. Access is checked on each resource, not just on Halo as a whole. ## Related - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) - [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md) --- ## What Governance Does Not Do Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-governance-does-not-do.md Governance answers one question: _is this person allowed to do this?_ It enforces access. It does not do the other jobs around it. | Governance does not… | Who does | | - | - | | **Log people in.** It does not check passwords or sign-ins. | CM.com sign-in (single sign-on). Governance receives the identity after the person has logged in. | | **Create users.** It copies user details from CM.com Platform. | CM.com Platform. | | **Create API keys.** It registers existing keys as [product tokens](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md). | CM.com Platform. | | **Store application data.** It holds no business data such as messages, contacts or reports. | The application. | | **Decide what an application's permissions are.** It stores and checks them. | The application's team. | ## What this means in practice - A person who can't log in has a sign-in problem, not an access problem. - If a permission is missing from the list of choices, the application has not defined it. - Governance tells an application "allow" or "deny". The application carries it out. ## Related - [What is Governance?](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-is-governance.md) - [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md) --- ## What is Governance? Source: https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-is-governance.md Governance is CM.com's central access management platform. It is the single source of truth for who can access what, and under which conditions. Applications ask Governance whether someone may do something, and Governance answers in real time. Access rules live in one place instead of being rebuilt in every application. See [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md). ## Who uses it - **Account admins** decide who gets which role in their account. - **App teams** define the permissions and roles of their application. - **Applications** ask Governance for access decisions, using the Governance client library. ## Core components - **Policy Information Engine (PIE)** stores roles, permissions and assignments. - **Policy Decision Engine (PDE)** evaluates access requests and makes authorization decisions. ## What it offers - **Authorization.** Governance decides whether a person has the permissions they need. See [How access decisions work](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/how-access-decisions-work.md). - **Roles and permissions.** Group permissions into roles, including custom roles for your organization. See [Roles](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/roles.md) and [Permissions](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/permissions.md). - **Role assignments.** Give a role to a person or a team, for an account or a whole organization, on specific resources if you want. See [Role assignments](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/role-assignments.md). - **Teams.** Create teams, give roles to a team, and every member gets them. See [Teams](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/teams.md). - **Resources.** Limit access to specific things inside an application. See [Resources](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/resources.md). - **User management.** User data is synced from the Platform service, and users can be invited. See [Principals](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/core-concepts/principals.md). - **Logs.** Access and change logs, which you can search and export as CSV. See [Audit logs](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/audit-logs.md). - **Client library.** Applications use it to ask Governance for decisions. ## Related - [What Governance does not do](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/what-governance-does-not-do.md) - [Getting started](https://docs.cm.com/governance/guides/getting-started.md) --- # Halo > Halo AI platform APIs for core operations and analytics. --- ## Analytics Source: https://docs.cm.com/halo/analytics.md Halo AI platform analytics APIs. --- ## Core Source: https://docs.cm.com/halo/core.md Core Halo AI platform APIs. --- ## Halo Source: https://docs.cm.com/halo.md Halo AI platform APIs for core operations and analytics. ## Explore --- ## Analytics API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/halo/analytics/v1/api-reference Base URL: `/halo` ### POST /analytics/v1/accounts/{account_id}/logging/feedback-scores Create a feedback score for a conversation interaction. Appmiral Ticketing API. --- ## Event Ticketing API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/live/event-ticketing/v1/api-reference Base URL: `https://api.cm.com/ticketing/v1` ### GET /customer-products List customer products for the organisation Returns all customer products (the individual tickets and other products issued to customers) across all of your events, including their barcode. Accepts the same filters as the event-level list. ### GET /events/ List events Returns your organisation's active events. ### POST /events/ Create event Creates a new event. `description` and `discount_label` are objects keyed by language code (for example `{"en": "...", "nl": "..."}`); provide them for the languages you list in `languages`. ### DELETE /events/{event_id} Delete event Deactivates an event: it is not removed, but `is_active` becomes `false`. Calling this on an event that is already inactive also returns `204`. ### GET /events/{event_id} View event Returns the details of one event, including its description and discount label in every language they are available in. ### PUT /events/{event_id} Edit event Replaces all editable fields of an event. This is a full replacement, not a partial update: send the complete event as you want it to be stored. Fields you leave out or set to `null`, and arrays you send empty, are cleared. ### GET /events/{event_id}/channels List channels Returns the active sales channels of an event. Each channel has a public shop `url` that you can link your customers to. ### GET /events/{event_id}/customer-products List customer products for an event Returns all customer products (the individual tickets and other products issued to customers) of one event, including their barcode. ### POST /events/{event_id}/discounts Create discount campaign Creates a discount campaign for an event. Set `discount_type` to choose the kind of discount. With `ORDER`, the discount applies to the whole order: provide a `rate`, a `rate_type` (`MONETARY` or `PERCENTAGE`) and the `discount_code` your customers will enter. With `PRODUCT`, the discount applies to specific products: provide `discount_campaign_products` with a `product_uuid`, `max_usage`, `rate` and `currency_id` for each product (each `rate_type` must be `MONETARY`); the discount code is generated for you. The response contains the campaign `id`, the `discount_code` (the one you supplied for `ORDER`, the generated one for `PRODUCT`) and the rate, or the per-product entries. ### PUT /events/{event_id}/discounts/{discount_id} Update discount campaign Updates the `name`, `max_usage`, `online_from` and `online_till` of a discount campaign. The rate, currency, discount code and per-product entries cannot be changed after the campaign is created; to change them, create a new campaign. The response has the same shape as the create response. ### GET /events/{event_id}/marketing-trackers List marketing trackers Returns the marketing trackers of an event, grouped by channel (shop). Each group has totals for clicks, orders and tickets sold, and lists its trackers with their own statistics and the tracking link to share. ### POST /events/{event_id}/marketing-trackers Create marketing tracker Creates a marketing tracker for one of your event's channels (shops). Pass the channel's `uuid`, as returned by `GET /events/{event_id}/channels`, as `viewport_uuid`. The tracker gets its own tracking link, so you can see how many clicks, orders and tickets each promotion brings in. Supported channels are `INSTAGRAM`, `FACEBOOK`, `TIKTOK`, `WHATSAPP`, `NEWSLETTER`, `X`, `SHOPIFY` and `OTHER`. The `SPOTIFY` and `AUTOMATED_EMAIL` channels are managed by CM.com and cannot be created here. ### DELETE /events/{event_id}/marketing-trackers/{tracker_id} Delete marketing tracker Deletes a marketing tracker. Only trackers that you created can be deleted; the `SPOTIFY` and `AUTOMATED_EMAIL` trackers are managed by CM.com and cannot be deleted. ### GET /events/{event_id}/orders List orders Returns the orders of an event, optionally filtered by status, product, sales origin or completion time. ### POST /events/{event_id}/orders Create order Creates an order for an event. There are two ways to use it. With `complete=true` the order is completed immediately, using the `payment_method` and `delivery_method` in the same request. With `complete=false` (the default) the order is created with status `PENDING` and reserves the requested tickets; you then finish it with `PUT /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/complete`, or release the tickets with `PUT /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/cancel`. The response has the same shape as `GET /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}`. Use `external_batch_id` to store your own reference for the order. ### GET /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id} View order Returns the details of one order: its status, the customer's details (name, contact details, address, organisation and date of birth; custom fields are not included), the payment method, the tickets that were ordered and the consents the customer gave. ### PUT /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/cancel Cancel order Cancels an order that is still `PENDING` and makes the tickets it reserved available again. This endpoint does not refund or cancel completed orders; to cancel individual tickets of a completed order, use the customer product cancel endpoint. Canceling an order that is already canceled returns `409`. ### PUT /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/complete Complete order Completes an order that was created with `complete=false` and is still `PENDING`. If you leave out `payment_method` it defaults to `FREE`, and if you leave out `delivery_method` it defaults to `NONE`. Completing an order that is already completed returns `409`. ### GET /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/products List customer products for an order Returns the customer products (the individual tickets and other products issued to the customer) of one order, including their barcode. Accepts the same filters as the event-level and organisation-level lists. ### GET /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/products/{customer_product_id} View customer product Returns the details of one customer product (an individual ticket or other product issued to a customer): its barcode, the customer's details, the product, the event and venue, the seat (`null` for events without seating), how often and when it was last scanned, and the tracking parameters of the order it belongs to. ### PUT /events/{event_id}/orders/{order_id}/products/{customer_product_id}/cancel Cancel customer product Cancels one customer product (an individual ticket or other product issued to a customer). Its barcode can no longer be used for entry and the product's stock is increased by one. The order it belongs to is not changed, and no refund is made. Canceling a customer product that is already canceled is not an error: the canceled customer product is returned. ### GET /events/{event_id}/payment-methods List payment methods Returns the payment methods that are enabled for an event and available to online customers. Box-office-only payment methods are not included. ### GET /events/{event_id}/products List products Returns the active products (for example tickets) of an event, with their name in each language and their price. ### GET /events/{event_id}/products/{product_id} View product Returns the details of one product, including its remaining `stock` (reported as 0 when `has_unlimited_stock` is `true`) and the `capacity` of the pool it draws from, which can be shared with other products. ### POST /events/{event_id}/reservations Create reservation Creates a reservation for the given event and immediately holds pool stock for every requested ticket. --- ## Event Ticketing: Partner API API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/live/ga-partner/v1/api-reference Base URL: `https://api.ticketing.cm.com/partnerapi/v1.0` ### POST /auth/signin Sign In ### POST /events/{event_uuid}/reservations/generate Generate Reservation This endpoint can be used to generate a reservation in your event. When the MAX_USAGE is null, the code can be used unlimited. ### GET /events/{event_uuid}/channels Get Channels ### GET /events/{event_uuid}/discountcampaigns/{discount_campaign_uuid} Patch Discount Campaign --- ## Memberships API endpoints (v1) API reference: https://docs.cm.com/live/memberships/v1/api-reference ### GET /api/v1/me Get the signed-in CM user Resolves the display name, first name, and email of the caller identified by the platform guard (JWT or the legacy CM SSO header). Returns 404 if the party or the address does not exist, or the address does not belong to the party. ### DELETE /api/v1/parties/{id}/addresses/{addressId} Cancel a pending address move Cancels a pending (strictly future-dated) address move by deleting that row outright, scoped to the tenant resolved from the request. Returns 404 if the party or the address does not exist, or the address does not belong to the party; returns 409 if the address is not a pending move (i.e. its `validFrom` is today or in the past). ### POST /api/v1/parties/{id}/addresses/move Move a party to a new address Closes a party's current address of a kind the day before `effectiveDate` and adds the new one from that date, scoped to the tenant resolved from the request. Returns 404 if the party does not exist or belongs to a different organisation, or has no current address of that kind yet (use `POST /addresses` for the first one); returns 409 if `effectiveDate` overlaps an existing address of that kind (e.g. another pending move). ### POST /api/v1/parties/{id}/notes Add a note to a party Appends a free-text note to a party, scoped to the tenant resolved from the request. the key is immutable.
